News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

News.title: The best bars and nightlife in Lyon
News.content:
While drinking in this gourmet city remains firmly rooted in the surrounding Rhône Valley’s ancient wine-growing heritage, new-gen addresses have embraced world cocktail culture in style. They’re using Lyon’s long-envied gastronomic know-how and rich bounty of local seasonal produce to create some sensational new drinks and food pairings as only the French can. Artisanal spirits meanwhile are increasingly fashionable: cornichon gin, Mezcal-fuelled soirées at chef Carla Kirsch’s gourmet tacos joint in Croix-Rousse, and the stunning Christian Drouin gin and pine-needle liqueur cocktail with stick of Comté cheese to stir I recently had at Hôtel Dieu’s Le Dôme bar all spring to mind.

Come the warmer days of spring and summer, the city’s fervent café-life spills onto pretty pavement terraces, while floating bars moored along Les Berges du Rhône (the landscaped river banks of the Rhône’s Rive Gauche or Left Bank) hum with after-dark dance parties and festivities. Clubbing remains fairly mainstream.

News.title: How to have the perfect holiday in France’s gastronomic capital
News.content:
Calling all bon vivants. This is your city. Within seconds of tucking into a traditional andouillette (tripe sausage) or modern vegetarian cuisine in a jam-packed bistro, admiring fine art in a Renaissance abbey, or getting delightfully lost in a traboule (secret passageway) used by 19th-century silk weavers, you’ll quickly realise that Lyon is a city that knows how to live well.

Enthralling, cinematic and richly storied, after living here for 10 years, I still find myself being surprised by a walled garden I never knew, a fresque (wall mural) suddenly popping up on a riverfront wall, a new museum or river boat route.

Street-smart Romans first spotted the city’s extraordinary topography, founding Lugdunum (Lyon’s predecessor) in 43BC on the sunny slopes of Fourvière. And to this day, this basilica-crowned hill above Lyon’s quaint Unesco-listed Old Town (Vieux Lyon) is the perfect perch for clocking the mighty Rhône and Saône rivers that wend their way so gracefully through the centre.

The city’s quays, landscaped with peaceful water gardens and floating bars, buzz night and day – while culture lovers can explore a bounty of museums. Then there’s the gastronomy: among France’s finest, thanks to the unfaltering creativity and sass of city chefs, both past and present.

News.title: The 16 best things to do in Lyon
News.content:
Few dedicated foodies make the pilgrimage to Lyon without dining once chez Paul Bocuse, be it at the late chef’s mythical, out-of-town gastronomic temple in Collonges-au-Mont d’Or (which lost one of its three stars in 2020, having held three since 1965) or at the more affordable Comptoir Paul Bocuse inside landmark covered market Halles de Lyon Paul Bocuse. Across the street, admire a larger-than-life portrait of the iconic chef, frescoed onto the side of a building. Inside the market, the moules glacées (cold mussel ‘soup’) at oyster and shellfish specialist Maison Merle and a gooey round of Saint Marcellin cheese from Fromagerie La Mère Richard are other local legends. Avoid buying fruit and veg here unless you have to – weekly outdoor food markets elsewhere in the city are cheaper.

To sample future talent in the Lyonnais kitchen, mingle with students over lunch, dinner or drinks and live music at La Commune – an innovative food court that hosts chefs aspiring to open their own restaurant in Lyon. Resident chefs cook up a storm at La Commune for maximum six months, meaning an ever-changing rollcall of epicurean excitement at this unique culinary incubator.

To extend the experience further afield, consider a road trip along a section of the Vallée de la Gastronomie, stretching 620km (385 miles). In Lyon, the gourmet route delves into the secrets behind chef Joseph Viola’s award-winning duck foie gras and sweetbread pâté en croûte (think French-posh pork pie) and the city’s distinctive offal-based bouchon (Lyonnais bistro) cuisine.

Sports.title: Newcastle urged to name St James’ Park stand after Kevin Keegan as Toon icon hails legend after his death at 75
Sports.content:
LES FERDINAND has called for Newcastle to pay Kevin Keegan the ultimate tribute by naming a stand after him at St James’ Park.

The Magpies legend passed away at the age of 75 earlier today, following a battle with cancer.



Newcastle icon Alan Shearer and other big names released emotional statements after the gut-wrenching news broke.

Ferdinand took his career to another level when he joined the Toon and notched 43 goals in 69 games under Keegan.



The former striker, 59, reckons Newcastle should rename one of their stands in honour of the two-time Ballon d’Or winner.

He told SunSport: “I really do hope they name one of the St James’ Park stands after Kevin because that would be a fitting tribute.

“What Kevin Keegan did for Newcastle United and the North East region as a whole will never be repeated.

“We will sit here and mourn him but, knowing Kevin, I know that instead he would want everyone to celebrate his life.”

Ferdinand was shocked by Keegan’s character after seeing him enjoy a glittering playing career with the likes of Liverpool and Hamburg.

The St James’ Park favourite added: “He’s the first superstar footballer I know.



“I remember watching him on the TV but when you met him, he was so humble, he was so charismatic.

“And he had a nice habit of just making you feel like a million dollars every time you were around him.

“I know how much he means to the North East and to Newcastle but, further afield, we should be paying him homage for what he’s done for football in general.



“My time with him was as a player at Newcastle so I know full well just how much he did for the region.”

Newcastle came agonisingly close to winning the Premier League title in 1996 and were runners-up again 12 months later.

Ferdinand conceded failing to be crowned champions is among his biggest regrets while on Tyneside.

The ex-Tottenham marksman admitted: “When I swapped QPR for Newcastle, it might have appeared to be a case of leaving the bright lights of London behind.

“But he somehow made the bright lights of Newcastle seem even brighter, if that makes sense. He certainly had a way with words.



“I think he was hell-bent on playing entertaining football and trying to entertain the paying public.

“The boys from that era will all agree we’re so sad we went so close to the top prize but ultimately weren’t able to secure the title for him.

“We enjoyed every minute of playing under him and he made it that way because of the brand of attacking football he wanted us to play.



“He wanted us to enjoy what we were doing and sometimes, as footballers, when you enjoy what you’re doing you’re going to play your best football, which is what we did the majority of the time.

“I think he’ll go down as producing one of the most entertaining teams that the Premier League has ever seen.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Normally people don’t remember who finished as the runners-up over the years, but they certainly remember our near miss.

“I don’t know whether that’s a good thing or a bad thing. But for that period of time, Newcastle were everyone’s second favourite team.”

Sports.title: Lamine Yamal dances wildly and Spain hero trolls Donald Trump as TWO MILLION fans line streets for World Cup bus parade
Sports.content:
LAMINE YAMAL showed off his dance moves on Spain’s open top bus parade while celebrating their World Cup triumph.

Spain returned home to Madrid as heroes this week after beating Argentina 1-0 in Sunday’s final.



The world champions arrived in the Spanish capital in a party mood after adding a second star to their shirt.

Luis de la Fuente’s men wasted little time kicking off the celebrations as they were welcomed back to Spain by a horde of adoring fans.





A total of TWO MILLION supporters lined the streets of Madrid with flags and banners and Barcelona ace Yamal lapped it up.

He enjoyed the scenes as he started dancing with Athletic Bilbao’s Nico Williams.

The 19-year-old performed a short improvised routine with the winger, who absolutely loved Yamal’s enthusiasm.

Some of his other Spain team-mates were topless while draping themselves in the national team flag and enjoying a few drinks.



And veteran striker Borja Iglesias decided to give himself the role as team DJ as he took to the decks to get the tunes going.

As the incredible atmosphere continued to build, some eagle-eyed fans noticed match-winning hero Ferran Torres was wearing a hilarious cap poking fun at Donald Trump.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The US President had just awarded the team their medals the previous day.

But Torres still took the opportunity to tease him as he wore a red cap that read: “Make Spain Great Again” – mimicking his trademark slogan for America.

Later on the Spain heroes all arrived on stage, with each one being given their own unique entrance music.

New Real Madrid man Marc Cucurella even started playing the drums during his performance.



Spain’s captain Rodri gave a speech to the fans while appearing on stage.

He said: “We’ve won the World Cup. And how many do we have? Two. These guys here are amazing, and I don’t know what else to say.

“I would like to remember a very important person to me, a player who has been unfairly criticized and who today is part of Spanish football history: Ferran.”

Manager De La Fuente added: “Thank you Spain for supporting us, for being here. We are lucky to have 26 fantastic people who are also fantastic footballers, the best in the world.



“For me, it is an honor to manage them and share this moment with my coaching staff. Together we are stronger, don’t forget that. Long live Spain!”

Sports.title: SunSport’s World Cup team of the tournament revealed including England star, wantaway Chelsea ace and veteran hero, 40
Sports.content:
THE World Cup is over with Spain emerging as winners after an incredible tournament.

Several big-name stars have delivered brilliant performances across the last six weeks in North America.



From the usual suspects, to new heroes, plenty of players have catapulted themselves to even greater stardom.

As the tournament winds down, SunSport’s Tom Barclay selects his team of the tournament…



GOALKEEPER: Vozinha, Cape Verde

BECAME an overnight social-media sensation for his stunning shutout against Spain at the start of the tournament.

That splendid display in the 0-0 stalemate against the eventual winners saw his following on Instagram skyrocket from 50,000 pre tournament to 29million.

The 40-year-old free agent also played well against Lionel Messi’s Argentina – surely someone will pick him up this summer?

RIGHT-BACK: Pedro Porro, Spain

THOSE who watched Tottenham scrap to Premier League survival on the final day of the season would not have predicted their two right-backs shining in the World Cup semi-finals.



But while Djed Spence’s heroics were not enough to see England get past Argentina, Porro scored the killer second goal as Spain shocked favourites France.

Porro was sensational all tournament and Spurs will be delighted they managed to tie him down to a bumper five-year contract midway through it.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

CENTRE-BACK: Pau Cubarsi, Spain

AN essential part of a miserly Spanish defence who kept seven clean sheets in eight games.



Playing alongside former Manchester City – and France – centre-back Aymeric Laporte, classy Cubarsi was the model of composure throughout and rightfully won the young player of the tournament award.

Another fantastic product from Barca’s La Masia academy, it is amazing to think he is still only 19.

CENTRE-BACK: Dayot Upamecano, France

DIDIER DESCHAMPS revealed on Friday that Upamecano is known as “the Little Monster” in the France set-up.



Harry Kane’s Bayern Munich team-mate followed up a fine season in the Bundesliga with an impressive tournament.

His speed and technical quality on the ball were key to France conceding only two goals in their first six games, before Luis de la Fuente’s Spain gave Les Bleus the blues.

LEFT-BACK: Marc Cucurella, Spain

CURLY-HAIRED Cucurella has had one heck of a summer.



On the day of Spain’s first game – when they were held to a 0-0 draw by plucky Cape Verde – it was announced the left-back was joining Real Madrid from Chelsea for £50million.

That sparked an excellent World Cup for the ex-Brighton man who was great going forward and a rock in defence as Spain emerged as champions.

DEFENSIVE MIDFIELD: Rodri, Spain

AFTER a season plagued by injury, the 2024 Ballon d’Or winner looked back to his best and took home the player of the tournament award.



Everyone in England knows his terrific ability to grip a game from the base of midfield and he was pivotal in helping Spain follow up their Euro 2024 win with glory here.

How Manchester City must be desperate to get a new contract sorted so they can pair him with £116m new-boy Elliot Anderson.

DEFENSIVE MIDFIELD: Enzo Fernandez, Argentina

THE man we love to hate – or maybe just hate.



But there is no denying the Argentina star is top quality and proved as much with that devastating late equaliser against England in that heartbreaking semi-final.

He massively let himself down in the final with his daft red card but until that point he was key to Argentina getting so close.

ATTACKING MIDFIELD: Michael Olise, France

COPPED a bit of flak for a quiet display against Spain in the semi-final.



But earlier in the tournament Olise was simply sensational, playing in a No10 role and displaying the kind of exquisite, defence-splitting passes that a peak Kevin De Bruyne would be proud of.

Another star Real Madrid have their eyes on this summer, though Bayern Munich team-mate Harry Kane will hope that possible blockbuster switch does not come off.

ATTACKING MIDFIELD: Jude Bellingham, England

WHAT an emphatic answer to anyone doubting him ahead of the tournament.



Kane was very good but Bellingham was unreal in the knockout games against Mexico and Norway, dragging England through with back-to-back braces.

He hit seven goals in total and was the Three Lions’ talisman. Argentina may have shackled him but it does not deny the fact he is a world-class operator who we are lucky to call our own.

STRIKER: Lionel Messi, Argentina

SOME of us had never seen Messi in the flesh until that fateful night in Atlanta – and then left wishing we had not.



The GOAT made a mockery of the fact he is turning 40 next summer by conjuring up two killer late goals to dump out England.

Not only that but he scored a whopping eight goals in the tournament, coming up clutch for the nation that adores him time and again.

STRIKER: Kylian Mbappe, France

MBAPPE wrote on social media that the France team had “failed” outgoing boss Didier Deschamps, who is stepping down after the tournament.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

That is after the tournament favourites were dumped out by Spain in the semis.

But that does not erase another excellent campaign individually by the Real Madrid mega star, whose 10 goals took him to 22 World Cup strikes overall and the golden boot.

Sports.title: England must SACK Thomas Tuchel if Pep Guardiola wants job – if he goes to Italy it will be the biggest miss of all time
Sports.content:
IT WOULD be easy for the FA to do nothing.

But if they do and see Pep Guardiola taking up the Italy offer being plotted by Paolo Maldini, they will regret it forever.



You can see the logic for sticking with Thomas Tuchel. After all, third was England’s best World Cup performance since 1966. It was the most successful of all time outside home soil.

England played, in the main, with a smile. And they ended with the broadest of grins – Miami, nice.



Tuchel, too, bristling at the stick he got for the semi-final surrender against Argentina, seemed to have rediscovered his mojo under the Florida sun while his players led the tributes to the spirit he has fostered.

But if the Wembley top brass had the courage of the convictions they claim, that the aim is to WIN Euros and World Cups, they should not settle for second best.



Guardiola – the world’s best manager, the man who reinvented football and fell in love with England – is available.

And that is a call a brave FA would make, today. Forget the cost of paying up Tuchel’s new two-year contract.

The FA have just banked £31million from the Fifa prize pot. They are not short of a few bob.

OK, if Guardiola isn’t up for it – despite soundings to the contrary – then stick with your king of clubs and seven of hearts.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But if he is, you have to twist.

Back Pep to be the four of diamonds to take you to 21. You can offer far more – in terms of players and readies, than a desperate Italian FA.

Tuchel is not a bad manager. He is a good manager. That’s crystal clear.

Yet “good” isn’t enough when you can get the pre-eminent coach and tactician of his generation.



Let’s be honest, even with Guardiola in the dugout in Atlanta, England might have lost to Argentina. But there is no way on earth they would have lost like THAT.

Surrendering the initiative, giving up the pitch, losing everything that had put them within touching distance of glory, inviting the inevitable.

While Pep looked washed out and ready for a long break at the end of last season, that won’t have lasted too long.

You can imagine him looking at all the signings made by Premier League clubs so far and wondering how they will work at Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Tottenham and his old club Manchester City – and how he would counteract them.

Even during his 12-month “sabbatical” in New York after leaving Barcelona, he was plotting and planning.



His fingers will be twitching already, his brain hot-wired. Which is why he has been willing to meet with Italy.

It may be that Guardiola wants an extended break. So if he fancies it from March, instead, OK.

We know Lee Carsley is a more than adequate caretaker. But England do not play a match of any real significance until June 2028.



Nobody is going to really care about the Nations League and even if they completely messed up qualification – which isn’t going to happen – they would still get through via Uefa’s back-door route for the hosts.

Indeed, even if there is no reaching out to Pep and Tuchel stays in charge, the situation could change by Christmas.

Atlanta has altered, negatively, the German’s relationship with the England fans. The feel-good factor is no more.

It means poor Wembley performances against Spain and then the Czech Republic in the autumn and it won’t just be paper aeroplanes flying around under the Arch.

There will be vitriol and animosity filling the air too.



Enough, perhaps, to make Tuchel also consider how much he wants to go through that for another 18 months – especially if a major club job becomes available. Should, for example, it not work out for Michael Carrick at Old Trafford.

Loyalty is a laudable thing in football with knee-jerk decision-making something to avoid.

But Guardiola has always been the FA’s No 1 target. The man they wanted.

Chief executive Mark Bullingham needs to pick up the phone and quickly.



Because if he is wearing Azzurri blue, not white, in the next few months, it will be the biggest miss of all time.

GOING SOUTH

THE fallout of Atlanta will not have been lost on Thomas Tuchel’s predecessor and his assistant.

Gareth Southgate and Steve Holland’s achievements of two finals, a semi and last-eight spot at major tournaments were forgotten in the FA’s scramble to endorse the German as the missing ingredient.

Then it turns out Tuchel deliberately chose to amplify and repeat everything the previous regime was accused of getting wrong.

It puts things in perspective, don’t you think?



GUNNER HURT

CHELSEA stealing Morgan Rogers from Arsenal’s grasp was a proper Premier League hijack.

Mikel Arteta will have every right to be hacked off, too. The Gunners manager must have assumed the move for the Aston Villa man was virtually a done deal.

But those fans at the Emirates who are moaning might remember how gleeful they were when they did the same thing to Spurs over Eberechi Eze last summer.



What goes around, comes around.

KEELY’S TOPS BUT KERR WAS EPIC

KEELY HODGKINSON deserves her status as Britain’s favourite track-and-field star.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But watching Josh Kerr demolish the mile world record on Saturday at the packed-out London Stadium was truly captivating.



It might even get some eyeballs on the Commonwealth Games when they start in Glasgow on Thursday.

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan was a God in Newcastle and his iconic ‘I would love it rant’ only made Geordies love him more
Sports.content:
WHEN Kevin Keegan netted twice against Newcastle to help Liverpool to a 3-0 victory in the 1974 FA Cup final, it seemed inconceivable that it would be on Tyneside where he became a football God.

Keegan was a great player for Liverpool, that is indisputable. Bought from lowly Scunthorpe, he was instrumental in not only that cup success but had already won the league title and Uefa Cup the year before.



And he went on to lift the league trophy twice more, another Uefa Cup and the European Cup before departing for German outfit Hamburg where he was a two-time European footballer of the year.

Yet despite such success, it was Newcastle where he truly became part of football folklore as both player and manager, despite never winning a major piece of silverware for one of the game’s sleeping giants.



It was a stunning moment to see Keegan unveiled as a shock new signing from high-flying Southampton, who had qualified for Europe in the old First Division.

He had also just returned from the 1982 World Cup with England and here he was pitching up at a club which had lost its way drifting around the second tier of English football playing in a dilapidated ground where fans had all but given up hope.

Keegan admitted it felt like coming home, because of his Geordie roots through his father, and that it had always been a dream of his to pull on the black and white shirt. As if he needed to endear himself to us anymore.

The local paper proclaimed “Let The Good Times Roll”, and fans queued round the block to witness his debut where, inevitably, he scored in a 1-0 triumph over QPR, throwing himself into the crowd in celebration.

By the end of 1984 Keegan had made sure the Magpies were back at football’s top table. He brought not just a club but a city back to life.

With promotion confirmed, Keegan scored in his final competitive appearance, a 3-1 victory over Brighton in front of an adoring 35,000 sellout crowd.



The other scorers that day were Peter Beardsley and Chris Waddle. What a forward line that was.

There was to be one more game for Keegan at St James’ Park, a testimonial against Liverpool and, ever the showman, it ended with him being whisked from the centre circle by helicopter.

We were drunk on Keegan mania and it left us with a heavy hangover when he departed.



By the time he returned, this time as manager eight years later, we were in an even worse place than when he’d arrived as a player.

Newcastle were in serious danger of being relegated to the third tier but, after briefly walking out claiming new owner John Hall hadn’t given him the transfer funds he expected, the pair made up and Keegan took Newcastle on an extraordinary journey.

He saved us from relegation, won the old First Division title a year later to get Newcastle into the recently formed Premier League and engineered a third place finish the following season.

By 1995/96, Newcastle appeared to be on the brink of their first top flight title since 1927.

The transformation was almost complete and we fans could almost touch English football’s biggest prize. The black and whites were 12 points clear and looked unstoppable.



But by March the lead was down to a single point and comparisons were being made with Devon Loch, the horse which was striding home, miles ahead in the 1956 Grand National only to stumble approaching the finish line and lose the race.

A 4-3 defeat at Liverpool, in what is regarded as one of the greatest Premier League games of all-time, saw Keegan slumped over an advertising hoarding as the realisation dawned that the dream was about to become a nightmare.

His famous Sky TV rant in which he exclaimed, “I would love it, love it, if we beat them” after Manchester United boss Alex Ferguson claimed teams were trying harder against the Red Devils than against Newcastle has gone down in the annals.



It made Keegan something of a joke figure to opposition football fans but not to us Geordies.

For us, it summed up his passion for our team and how desperate he was to succeed.

Of course we missed out on the title and Manchester United triumphed but King Kev’s Great Entertainers have never been forgotten.

They won legions of fans up and down the country and around the world for the fantastic football they played.

Keegan tried to push on by breaking the world transfer record when he splashed out £15million to sign local hero Alan Shearer from Blackburn.



And while there was a small semblance of satisfaction in a 5-0 home crushing of Fergie’s United, by January 1997 Keegan had quit claiming he couldn’t take the club any further.

Hall tried to talk him out of it but there was an understanding from fans, players and owner that Keegan had given his all and was burnt out by the whole experience.

After spells managing Fulham, England and Manchester City where, on leaving he announced that he would never manage again, he made a shock return to St James’ Park as boss in January 2008.



But it was to be a short-lived second coming. Keegan never saw eye-to-eye with new owner Mike Ashley, and felt he was having players that he didn’t want imposed on him. It was no huge surprise when he quit eight months later.

But that did not tarnish Keegan’s legacy for us.

On the day his cancer diagnosis was revealed, the big screen at St James’ Park put up the message “We’re all with you King Kev” as the crowd loudly sang about Walking in a Keegan Wonderland, something we did for so many unforgettable years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES



That night Newcastle were on the right side of a 4-3 victory against Leeds. It was as if Keegan had ordered a special show in his own honour.

His journey may be over but Kevin Keegan will live forever in the hearts and minds of the Geordie nation.

Sports.title: Tynan Thompson deal from Tottenham for £8m could pave way for Man Utd’s biggest transfers
Sports.content:
THE ONLY Manchester United starters against Wrexham yet to play a full international were Leny Yoro, Ayden Heaven and Jack Fletcher.

Heaven and Fletcher are both 19 and Yoro turned 20 last November. United’s line-up would have been more senior had Benjamin Sesko and Matthijs de Ligt not been injured.



United have improved their squad, if not their starting team, with their three incomings. Karl Darlow is a better back-up goalie than Altay Bayindir, while Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans can be assured of ample playing time but neither are a nailed-on starter when Saturday or Sunday comes.

Investing £85m on two midfielders rather than on one who suffered successive relegations was prudent. A game-changing midfielder has eluded United so far this summer, though, and they require an imposing partner for Kobbie Mainoo.



Santos and Tielemans will not suffice. They provide a good blend of youth and experience and both are preferable to the underwhelming Ederson who United prioritised before last season had even ended.

The concept of a ‘best XI’ is borderline obsolete these days. All three of Arsenal’s major summer signings – Viktor Gyokeres, Martin Zubimendi and Eberechi Eze – were on the bench for the Champions League final.

Yet Michael Carrick earned a two-year contract as United head coach through little or no changes to his starting XI on a weekly basis.

Carrick named an unchanged team four times. The most changes he made to a side before United qualified for the Champions League were the four in the defeat to Leeds United, United’s worst performance under Carrick.

The five alterations at Sunderland in May resulted in the only time Carrick’s United fired blanks. Tellingly, the misfiring Joshua Zirkzee replaced Benjamin Sesko.

That afternoon remains Zirkzee’s only start this calendar year. Carrick had some joy with Bryan Mbeumo at centre forward as he scored five times there, despite also enduring a three-month goal drought.

Zirkzee could linger at United as Sesko is not match-fit. He could miss a chunk of pre-season with the shin injury that caused him to miss United’s final three fixtures last term.



But Zirkzee is merely a body. Mbeumo, Cunha, Amad and Bruno Fernandes are more appealing options as false nines than the Dutchman.

United last week denied that they had informally approached Danny Welbeck about a possible return. A wily and wiry back-up striker is needed to support Sesko and settling for Zirkzee would not be progressive.

A left winger has arrived, although the 18-year-old Tynan Thompson is not expected to be promoted to the first team straight away.

United did promise Thompson that he would be integrated into the senior squad and suddenly he is their only specialist option there.

Marcus Rashford remains a United player for now but there is doubt he will pull on the red shirt again. The next three weeks, essentially Rashford’s post-World Cup holiday, are particularly crucial as they are the last that Rashford remains away from United.



Ruben Amorim is long gone and Carrick spent nearly six years as Rashford’s teammate, coach and caretaker manager. Carrick is so unconfrontational his only red card was for accidentally kicking the ball away against AC Milan.

But the head coach no longer dictates recruitment at United. Accommodating their highest earner who last played for the club in December 2024 and has publicly stressed his wish to leave permanently is not an outcome United can countenance.

Rashford should not be a hard sell. He is available for less than £30m, started at the World Cup, won the league with Barcelona last season and spent nearly nine years as a regular at United.



Options are limited, though. Turkey or Saudi Arabia do not appeal as Rashford wants to safeguard his England place and only a handful of clubs could afford his salary.

Aston Villa, flush with nearly £150m from Tielemans and Morgan Rogers, but squeezed by Uefa’s financial fair play rules and profitability and sustainability, could do worse than to re-sign Rashford. This time permanently.

Well-placed sources said United would “pause” after the flurry of incomings last week as sales have to be addressed.

If United sell Rashford for around £25m, £325,000 will be cleared off the weekly wage bill to go with the £38m for Rasmus Hojlund and the £12m sell-on fee banked from Mason Greenwood’s transfer to Fenerbahce. Alejandro Garnacho could bring in more income if or when he is sold by Chelsea.

That gives United plenty of headroom to bring in a headline midfielder and a worthy second striker without straying close to the extreme fees that Manchester City, Tottenham and Chelsea have paid.



United have shown they are prepared to deviate from their strategy with the 29-year-old Tielemans, older than their preferred targets. Raising the age of a signing pales in comparison to raising the price and United rightly scoffed at the £85m valuation of Mateus Fernandes.

They need to lay down a marker, though. Cunha and Mbeumo were prised from selling clubs but there was firm competition for both. United paid sensible but striking fees of £62.5m and £65m rising to £71m for Premier League pedigree.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Newcastle were interested in Sesko and had the Champions League to offer. As long as Sesko remains unavailable, United look blunt at the tip of the arrow.

And Zirkzee is an international.

Sports.title: Hilarious moment Spanish pilot plays ‘sick joke’ fooling plane full of Argentina fans into thinking they’d won World Cup
Sports.content:
THIS is the hilarious moment when a Spanish pilot appeared to fool a plane full of Argentinian passengers into believing they had won the World Cup.

Ferran Torres came off the bench to grab an extra-time winner last night, leaving Lionel Messi and Co heartbroken.



And footage, which was recorded straight after Spain were crowned world champions for a second time, is going viral.

Fans wearing Argentina shirts were filmed jumping up and down with excitement after being given the fake news over the tannoy on a night flight.



The plane fell silent as the pilot said: “It was a fiercely contested match right to the end, including extra-time.

“Both teams gave it their all but, unfortunately, only one team can win the World Cup final.”



He went on to unleash a wave of jubilation by adding: “We wanted to congratulate our Argentinian friends.”

But, in a second part of the video posted online, the plane fell silent when the pilot revealed: “Spain has won.”

Argentinian media outlets did not see the funny side, with some describing the announcement as a “sick joke.”

Newspaper La Voz del Interior wrote: “During a flight, as the World Cup was reaching its climax, a Spanish captain announced a false result that sparked celebrations among the passengers before revealing Spain were the champions.”



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Another Argentinian news outlet, branding the pilot’s actions as “terrible”, said: “Not only did he commit a terrible act with a questionable sense of humour, but he exposed himself to serious consequences aboard the aircraft once the truth finally came out.

“The passengers might have wanted to confront him or enter the cockpit. A massive blunder.”

The name of the airline and the plane’s destination has not yet been made public.

Argentina had to play the whole of extra-time with ten men after Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez was sent off.



And members of the South American giants’ squad failed to control their anger when their dreams of retaining the World Cup were ended.

Leandro Paredes saw red for his part in a mass brawl following the final whistle.

The scrap erupted after Nahuel Molina appeared to throw a punch at Spanish captain Rodri.



Fifa chiefs have launched a formal investigation into the ugly scenes at the end of the showdown.

Sports.title: England World Cup ratings: Jude Bellingham silences doubters with elite performances but Arsenal and Chelsea stars flop
Sports.content:
ENGLAND notched their best finish at a World Cup since 1966 – but some members of the squad still failed to live up to expectations.

The Three Lions bagged the bronze medal after a thrilling 6-4 victory over France last night.



And Thomas Tuchel’s side have already jetted back into England having boarded a flight straight after their win in Miami.

A string of big names shone as they chased glory at the summer extravaganza.



That includes Jude Bellingham, who bagged a record-breaking SEVEN goals at the tournament.

SunSport’s Tom Barclay has rated each member of the squad who were handed game time at the World Cup…



JORDAN PICKFORD: 6/10

Mixed fortunes for what is now the England player with the most World Cup appearances ever. Dubbed ‘Jordan Banks’ for his amazing save and performance in the Azteca, he looked jumpy and flappy in other games – while he perhaps could have done better with Enzo Fernandez’s killer leveller against Argentina. Bellingham seemed to think so.

DEAN HENDERSON: 6

Finally got a chance to show what he could do in that bonkers third-place play-off. He pulled off some decent stops in that madcap match but still conceded four.

REECE JAMES: 4

Tuchel seemed to be the only person in the world who did not foresee James picking up a hamstring injury at this tournament. Everyone else’s fears came to pass as the Chelsea captain succumbed to his crock curse yet again – and even when he did play, did not play anywhere near as well as we know he can do.

EZRI KONSA: 7

Appeared to be the one defender Tuchel was relying on until he benched him for the biggest match against Argentina. But overall Konsa acquitted himself pretty well, especially in that Alamo, ten-man effort against Mexico in the Azteca. Netted in the 6-4 bronze clash.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

NICO O’REILLY: 6

In and out at left-back which was perhaps not that surprising given he is not really a left-back. Or at least he was not for most of last season under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City. There were moments of promise in the 21-year-old’s first tournament and hopefully much more to come from one of our most talented youngsters.

JOHN STONES: 7

Shaky start against Croatia saw him dropped, but then the 32-year-old really came to the fore in the knockout stages. Superb in shackling old mucker Erling Haaland in the quarter-final against Norway, Stones became the first-ever free agent to play for England.

MARC GUEHI: 7

Had to win over doubting Tuchel after being benched for the first game, but was an ever-present after that. Put his body on the line when required and is a reliable performer – but there are question marks if he will ever reach the levels of a John Terry, Rio Ferdinand or Stones.

DAN BURN: 7

Big Dan Burn justified his slightly controversial call-up with a couple of eye-catching cameos off the bench. His crunching header which left Norway’s Leo Ostigard in a heap will live long in the memory, but the 34-year-old also embodies Tuchel’s back-five park-the-bus approach.

TREVOH CHALOBAH: 5

Drafted in at the last minute following Tino Livramento’s injury which ruled the Newcastle man out for the tournament. Only action he saw was the final few minutes of the 6-4 win against France, but there was still time for him to be put on his backside by Ousmane Dembele as the PSG man netted.



DJED SPENCE: 8

The breakout star for Tuchel’s England that no one predicted. Spence struggled to get a game for Roberto De Zerbi towards the end of Spurs’ Premier League season – where they finished 17th – but he was excellent in North America, full of running, tackles and passion.

JARELL QUANSAH: 4

Most memorable contribution was being sent off against Mexico for his high challenge on Jesus Gallardo. That saw him cop a two-match ban – which felt ridiculous given the Folarin Balogun farce – but when he did come back against France, he was given a torrid time by Kylian Mbappe and Bradley Barcola. Penny for Trent Alexander-Arnold’s thoughts.

DECLAN RICE: 5

He was excellent against France but, if we’re honest, the pressure was off then. For the rest of the tournament, Rice was not his usual inspirational and dynamic self. Fitness was clearly the issue due to a neural problem in his hamstring going back to December – plus he was in bed with a sickness bug for three days before Norway.



ELLIOT ANDERSON: 7

The discovery of the Tuchel era was good throughout the tournament. Manchester City’s new £116million signing only made his England debut ten months ago but he looked like he had been playing for his country for years, showing energy, demanding the ball and having no fear of going in hard on Lionel Messi.

JUDE BELLINGHAM: 9

A breathtaking tournament for the Real Madrid superstar, making those who questioned how much Tuchel needed him look silly. Seven goals is the most by an England player at a World Cup and the only reason he does not get ten is because of how Argentina kept him quiet.

JORDAN HENDERSON: 5

This score may be a bit harsh but sadly Henderson’s biggest ‘on-field’ moment came when he broke his arm falling over advertising hoardings at the Azteca, ruling himself out of action from then on. But you only have to hear Bellingham speak to see what an influence the 36-year-old is on the dressing room.

MORGAN ROGERS: 5

Chelsea are splashing £117m on him and he is a very good player but his tournament was meh at best. Biggest contribution – and it was a vital one – was his excellent cross for Anthony Gordon’s goal against Argentina. But not a lot to write home about apart from that.



EBERECHI EZE: 6

Eze sparkled against France, teeing up Bukayo Saka’s second and had one mazy run that really caught the eye. But again, that game had more of a feel of an exhibition, despite the bronze medal being up for grabs. When the real pressure was on, Eze’s few cameos off the bench were pretty forgettable, as Cole Palmer and Phil Foden may well have noted.

BUKAYO SAKA: 5

This score may seem extraordinary given Saka scored a hat-trick against France. But the question we all had after that treble was ‘Where was this earlier in the tournament, when it really mattered?’ Surely injury played a part but Saka insisted he was fit and grumbled about not being picked against Argentina. The fact is if he was playing anywhere near the level of the play-off game earlier in the competition, he would have been a nailed-on starter for the semi. Sadly, he wasn’t.

HARRY KANE: 8

Another fine campaign from England’s record-scorer, who took his tally up to 84 with six more World Cup goals. Without doubt his best moment was digging us out the mire against DR Congo with a late brace, but he had very little impact against Argentina, leading golf buddy Donald Trump to question why the striker had been used as “a defensive player”.

MARCUS RASHFORD: 6

Took his goal brilliantly off the bench in the opener against Croatia but then blew hot and cold for the rest of the tournament. Lost the left-wing battle to Gordon – the man who took his place at Barcelona – but did well in that blistering first 45 minutes against France.



ANTHONY GORDON: 8

If this was a ranking for the group stages, Barca new-boy Gordon would probably get a four. But he was so effective in the knockouts with three assists, a penalty won against Mexico and the goal in the loss to Argentina, that those contributions massively outweigh the early fixtures. Why oh why did Tuchel take him off in that semi-final?

OLLIE WATKINS: 5

Opportunities severely limited for the Aston Villa man, as they always will be as Kane’s back-up. Struggled when coming on against France in the play-off, though was playing out of position out wide, in fairness.

NONI MADUEKE: 3

Given far more opportunities than perhaps many expected because of Saka’s struggles with form and fitness. But he failed to take them, showing poor end product and predictability. Being hooked at half-time against Norway was the nadir and he did not play another minute after.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

IVAN TONEY: 5

Laboured against France in that play-off game, looking off the pace after six weeks without competitive action – barring the final few minutes against Argentina as a Hail-Mary substitute which did not work.

THOMAS TUCHEL: 4

On the one hand, Tuchel masterminded our best World Cup since they won it in 1966. But on the other – and what every fan will remember most – he presided over England snatching defeat from the jaws of victory in the semi-final against Argentina thanks in large part to his ultra-defensive strategy. Tuchel was brought in at great expense to get us over the line and he failed to do so.

Sports.title: World Cup final: FIFA investigation launched after disgraceful Argentina throw punches at Spain stars
Sports.content:
Spain have been crowned world champions but the behaviour of Argentina at the final whistle has led to calls for Fifa to ban several players - follow all the reaction

Spain are world champions, beating a bad-tempered Argentina 1-0 in New Jersey in the final.

Ferran Torres's extra time winner came after nearly two hours of goalless football at MetLife Stadium and with Argentina reduced to 10 men by Chelsea's Enzo Fernandez getting sent off for two bookable offences.

At the final whistle, a huge brawl kicked off, triggered by Leandro Paredes attacking a number of Spain players including Rodri, Eric Garci and Gavi - with Paredes sent-off for throwing punches and kicking out.

There have been calls for Fifa to "throw the book" at Argentina, who also turned their backs on Spain receiving their medals and lifting the trophy in another poor act of sportsmanship.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez breaks silence after World Cup final red card with message to Argentina fans
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez breaks silence after World Cup final red card with message to Argentina fans

After he was sent off for Argentina in the World Cup final, Enzo Fernandez has released a social media post explaining his thoughts

View 2 Images Referee Slavko Vincic shows a red card to Enzo Fernandez of Argentina (Image: Heuler Andrey/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Argentina midfielder Enzo Fernandez has broken his silence after being sent off in the World Cup final. The Chelsea ace was booked for dissent in the second half and then shown a second yellow card for a reckless challenge on Spain defender Pau Cubarsi.

‌



His dismissal resulted in Argentina having to play 30 minutes of extra time with only 10 men. Spain struggled to take advantage but eventually won the game through Ferran Torres' crisp half volley in the penalty area.

‌



Before his red card, Fernandez was at the heart of Argentina's World Cup campaign, heading in the winning goal against Egypt and scoring a crucial equaliser in their 2-1 win over England. However, after his red card, he sent a message to his followers on social media.

‌



Just over 24 hours after his dismissal, the Chelsea midfielder took to social media and wrote: "As time goes by, you realise there is something much bigger than just a result. For years, this group has represented us in the best possible way.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"It teaches that competing isn't just about winning; it's about giving your all for the jersey and never giving up. It has been a privilege to be part of a group that always stepped up, competed at the highest level, and defended these colours with pride, humility, and commitment.

‌



"I want to thank all the Argentine fans. Thank you for always being there, for supporting us in every match, for the affection, for the unconditional support, and for making us feel at home anywhere in the world.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

"Wearing my country's jersey is the greatest honour of my career, and I will continue to give my all every time I get to defend it."

‌



Throughout the tournament, he contributed two goals in seven appearances in the USA, Canada and Mexico. He also played every minute of every game for Lionel Scaloni's side, up until his red card at the New York/New Jersey Stadium.

View 2 Images Enzo Fernandez was sent off for Argentina in extra time (Image: Getty Images)

Fernandez has been widely chastised by pundits for his sending off. His showing of dissent towards referee Slavko Vincic was a costly and unnecessary booking, while his second challenge on Cubarsi was high, late, and could arguably have put him in danger of seeing a straight red card.

Article continues below

He was also heavily criticised by his country's media after the match. Argentine outlets La Nacion and Ole both ranked him a 4/10, while Clarin gave him a five before summarising his display by saying: "The sending-off capped off one of his worst matches of the tournament."

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola in talks to make managerial return after opening door to England job
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola in talks to make managerial return after opening door to England job

Pep Guardiola is understood to be keen on managing England in the future despite changing his mind over taking the job back in 2024 - but he is now being targeted by another nation

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola is being courted by the Italian football federation (Image: Oscar Del Pozo/AFP)

Italy have held talks with Pep Guardiola in a bid to persuade the former Manchester City boss to become their next manager, it has been claimed.

‌



The Italians are in desperate need of reform after failing to qualify for three consecutive World Cup finals, with Gennaro Gattuso agreeing to leave his post as head coach after Italy's disappointing defeat in the qualifying play-offs against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

‌



Their search for a new manager has seemingly taken them to the door of Guardiola, who has previously opened the door to managing a national team.

‌



Guardiola, 55, left Manchester City at the end of the 2025-26 campaign after a decade at the helm and has played down talk that he could resume his managerial career sooner rather than later.

Lionel Messi shows true colours with emotional message after World Cup final loss READ MORE :

However, The Times report that Paolo Maldini, acting in his new role as technical director of the Italian football federation, held talks over three days with Guardiola in Barcelona at the weekend with his adviser, Leonardo.

Maldini and Leonardo are said to have a good relationship with Guardiola, who would be regarded as a major coup for Italy if he can be enticed into succeed Gattuso.

‌



Guardiola's salary is likely to be an obstacle in any bid to make him Italy's next manager, though, with the Catalan coach's demands likely to be far more significant than any previous incumbents.

View 2 Images Italy failed to qualify for the World Cup again this summer and want Guardiola to be their next manager (Image: Claudio Villa/FIGC)

Interest in Guardiola comes just days after it emerged that he had a verbal agreement with the Football Association to become England's next manager following Gareth Southgate's decision to stand down from his post after Euro 2024.

‌



However, Guardiola subsequently had a rather dramatic change of heart and ended up staying at Manchester City for two more years.

Guardiola is said to have expressed a desire to manage England in the future to those close to him. The position is currently held by Thomas Tuchel, who the FA turned to after Guardiola's U-turn, but the German has been heavily scrutinised over the manner of England's crushing World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Though there is bitterness over England's decision to drop deep after taking the lead against Argentina, Tuchel did guide the Three Lions to their best finish at a World Cup finals since their triumph back in 1966 as a result of beating France 6-4 in the bronze final.

Sports.title: Huge World Cup 2030 change already confirmed as football chief 'leaks' announcement
Sports.content:
Huge World Cup 2030 change already confirmed as football chief 'leaks' announcement

The 2026 World Cup only recently ended with Spain winning the competition, but a huge change to the 2030 competition was seemingly confirmed by one FIFA official

View 2 Images The focus is already being paid to the 2030 World Cup (Image: 2026 FIFA)

CONMEBOL President Alejandro Dominguez has seemingly confirmed FIFA will expand the 2030 World Cup to 64 teams. The confetti has barely stopped falling in the USA since Spain overcame Argentina in a fiery final in New York.

‌



However, attention is already being shifted to the centenary competition, which is mainly grounded in Spain, Morocco and Paraguay, but will also have fixtures taking place in Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay. FIFA president Gianni Infantino recently opened the door to another expansion, with the recent tournament in the USA, Canada and Mexico being the first to feature 48 teams instead of the usual 32.

‌



However, while the Swiss boss made it clear plenty needs to be considered before the competition can be expanded again, Dominguez, who is the head of South America's answer to UEFA, appeared to confirm 64 nations will feature in 2030, despite no official word from FIFA being issued.

‌



Get the latest World Cup news straight to your inbox by signing up to our Make Football Great Again newsletter now!

Not long after the final, Dominguez took to X and wrote: " The next one is played at home! In 2030, the World Cup comes to Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay, a great opportunity for soccer, to celebrate the Centenary of the World Cup with a competition featuring 64 teams."

The day before, he uploaded a similar tweet ahead of the World Cup final. However, his tone was significantly less certain compared to his recent post.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

He wrote: " We are living through a historic World Cup, the first with 48 teams, a true success. Congratulations dear Gianni Infantino and to all the friends at FIFA for such a great organisation, and congratulations Spain for being the new world champion.

"In 2030, we'll see you at home with the dream of playing it with 64 teams to celebrate the centenary of the World Cup!"

‌



Content cannot be displayed without consent

His choice of words in the first tweet he issued, stating the 64-team format is a "dream" at this point, suggests it's still a considering at the current moment. That mirrors what Infantino said when first asked about the 64-team competition.

Infantino, when asked about it, said to Blue Sport: "These are all issues that we will be examining after the World Cup. When organising a World Cup, it's important to organise it for the whole world - not just Europe and South America, but effectively the entire world.

‌



View 2 Images Dominguez (right) seemingly confirmed the next World Cup will have 64 teams (Image: 2026 FIFA)

"Every nation should be allowed to dream of participating in the World Cup. You can see that the quality of the teams is extremely high, and it's getting higher and higher, all over the world. If you don't give smaller countries a chance to participate in the World Cup, they'll lack the incentive to keep improving."

The 64-team format has not received complete support, as UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin described it as a "bad idea" while Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al Khalifa, the president of the Asian Football Confederation, believed it would cause "chaos" in international football.

Sports.title: UEFA president 'boycotts' World Cup final after Donald Trump and FIFA outrage
Sports.content:
UEFA president 'boycotts' World Cup final after Donald Trump and FIFA outrage

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin was not at the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina

View 2 Images UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin (R) was not at the World Cup final due to a reported breakdown in relationship with FIFA. (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin reportedly boycotted the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina 'in protest' against FIFA after a breakdown in relations between the two governing bodies. Ceferin, who also serves as FIFA vice-president, was notably absent from the showpiece finale yesterday.

‌



While Donald Trump and several other high profile figures attended the game, Ceferin was nowhere to be seen. The Times claims the Slovenian's absence was a result of the Folarin Balogun saga, which saw FIFA suspend a red card offence for the United States striker after he was sent off, meaning he was eligible to play against Belgium.

‌



UEFA released a damning statement in the aftermath of FIFA's decision, which read: "Yesterday’s decision to suspend for a probationary period of a year the implementation of the one-match automatic suspension following the red card issued to the player Folarin Balogun crossed a red line.

‌



UEFA's five major issues with FIFA World Cup as president snub highlights divide READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"Football, like any other sports, relies on rules, which are the basis for fair, honest and transparent competition. Sometimes rules are open to interpretation. In this case not. A minimum automatic suspension of one match following a red card is not a discretionary option and does not require the decision of a competent body to be enacted.

"It is a principle embedded in regulations, which cannot be made subject to exceptions, let alone in the middle of a tournament where several other players have been in the same situation and regularly served their suspension.

‌



"When the certainty of rules is no longer guaranteed by its guardians, the integrity of the game is at stake and the credibility of a competition is undermined. Equally, such decision creates a precedent in the ongoing tournament, where similar situations will now require an equal treatment, to the detriment of the competition.

"Football is the most loved sport in the world because it is a beautiful game and is trusted because it is played everywhere with the same laws.

"A tournament is never a pure standalone and, if the tournament in question is the World Cup, it has the power to drive positive or negative consequences on the game as a whole. We express our disbelief at such an unprecedented, incomprehensible and unjustifiable decision."

‌



View 2 Images UEFA president Alexander Ceferin and FIFA boss Gianni Infantino (Image: Masashi Hara, Getty Images)

It's not the only major decision that FIFA have made in recent months to upset the UEFA chief. Those include the proposed expansion of the World Cup to 64 teams, half-time shows and high ticket prices for the tournament.

There was also a debacle surrounding Somalian referee Omar Artan, who was denied entry to the US before the tournament started. After that decision, UEFA installed him as the official as referee for the Super Cup match between PSG and Aston Villa later this summer.

Article continues below

There have also been murmurings throughout the summer that UEFA could pitch a candidate to run against Gianni Infantino at the next FIFA presidential election, with the Italian previously thought to be running unopposed.

The current FIFA head-honcho has outlined his intention to run for a third campaign, but there is growing support for other candidates within UEFA.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi shows true colours with emotional message after World Cup final loss
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi shows true colours with emotional message after World Cup final loss

Argentina came up short in their bid to win back-to-back World Cups and their captain and talisman Lionel Messi has broken his silence following the defeat to Spain

View 2 Images Lionel Messi has spoken after Argentina's World Cup final loss (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

Lionel Messi has penned an open letter to Argentina supporters following their unsuccessful bid to become just the third team in history to win successive World Cups.

‌



Messi and Co went into Sunday's final with Spain as the defending champions after victory in Qatar back in 2022. But Argentina were very much second best against Luis de la Fuente's side, who dominated from start to finish. Ferran Torres plundered the only goal of the game in extra-time after Enzo Fernandez had been sent off for a moment of madness in the final minutes of regulation time.

‌



At 39 years of age, there is every chance Sunday's final in New Jersey was Messi's final World Cup appearance.

‌



The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner broke down after the game when he was serenaded by Argentina fans. Nearly 24 hours later, he has taken to social media to speak about the pain of said defeat, while also congratulating Spain on their win.

World Cup final LIVE: FIFA investigation launched after disgraceful Argentina throw punches at Spain stars READ MORE :

UEFA's five major issues with FIFA World Cup as president snub highlights divide READ MORE :

“The pain is immense, it will take time for this wound to heal. But I also choose to hold on to all the good things, all matches we turned around by giving everything and moments that will remain in our memories forever.

“I will always remember the support of an entire country that, together with the work and effort of this group, brought us back once again among the best teams in the world.

‌



“Today, it is difficult to appreciate what we achieved… but this group has really reached two consecutive World Cup finals. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and every message. Once again, we managed to come together as a country and stand united, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.

View 2 Images Messi was devastated after the final whistle (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

“I also want to congratulate Spain on winning World Cup.”

‌



The aftermath of the World Cup final was marred by ugly scenes as Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes both lashed out at opponents.

Wayne Rooney condemned their actions, saying: “Does it surprise you? It doesn't surprise me. We've seen this with Argentina before.

“It's just not the reaction you want. We've seen some of the reaction after knocking England out in the last round. That's just sad. If you lose a game of football, be graceful and get out of there. It's really poor from them.”

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan: Newcastle and Liverpool legend dies aged 75 as tributes pour in
Sports.content:
It has been confirmed that Kevin Keegan, the Newcastle and Liverpool legend, has sadly died at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer

Kevin Keegan has sadly passed away at the age of 75 following a battle with cancer, his family have announced.

It was confirmed back in January that the legendary former Newcastle manager was being treated for cancer, with Keegan himself revealing the disease was at stage four last month during an appearance at a fan event.

A statement released by Keegan's family on Monday afternoon read: "It is with immense sadness that we announce that Kevin Keegan has passed away at the age of 75. The former England player and manager had been battling cancer and was surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments.

"Kevin, a double Ballon D’or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather. The family would like to thank Kevin’s incredible medical team for all their support. "This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

Sports.title: Menzies shocks world No 2 Humphries in World Matchplay thriller
Sports.content:
Cameron Menzies produced a massive upset to defeat 2024 champion Luke Humphries 10-7 at the World Matchplay on Monday night.

World No 2 Humphries took centre stage against one of the most entertaining and unpredictable players in the game in Menzies.

And it was the Scot who raised the Empress Ballroom roof with an inspired 170 checkout to stun the former world champion and seal his first win on the Winter Gardens stage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies lands 'The Big Fish' to stun Luke Humphries at the World Matchplay

Betfred World Matchplay - Monday's results

Round Two

Ross Smith 10-6 Kevin Doets Gerwyn Price 11-9 Martin Schindler Cameron Menzies 10-7 Luke Humphries Rob Cross 10-3 Danny Noppert

Menzies produced a brilliant double-double 129 finish to lead Humphries 3-2, but 'Cool Hand' made it six consecutive breaks of throw with a magnificent 167 checkout to level straight after the first interval.

Menzies then went on a blistering four-leg burst to race into a 7-3 lead but could only win one out of the next five legs as Humphries went on a charge.

However, Menzies landed an inspired 170 checkout to cause a mighty shock as he set up a second-round clash with Ross Smith.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Humphries pinned this stunning 167 on the bull

"No one gave me hope! I didn't give myself hope but I finally won a game at the Winter Gardens," said a delighted Menzies.

"Luke Humphries is a great guy, a great player. At 7-3 I was just trying not to think of that finishing line but the nerves kicked in. To beat Humphries, I know he will be disappointed. He gave me a lot of stress at doubles but that's my biggest win.

"I show a lot of emotion and I hate that I do that. I'm trying to keep myself intact. Try to keep myself composed because I know he was going to have a spell and batter me and he had a little spell but lucky enough I had that lead.

"I know that's not Humphries but I'll take it any day of the week."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Menzies hits this HUGE double-double finish against Humphries

Mardle: Menzies' greatest moment - he knows he can handle anything now

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hear from Menzies and Wayne Mardle after the Scotsman claimed a famous win over Humphries

"It's his best ever win, and he mentioned that," said Wayne Mardle, speaking to Sky Sports.

"With Cameron Menzies, everyone mentions his emotions, but it's the way he had to win that game.

"Nothing went according to plan. He was broken back early twice, that's up-and-down emotions. The high of breaking to being broken back.

"Then he went on a run, and got pegged back. There was a lot happening in that game, but he held it all together beautifully.

"Humphries had an amazing spell of four legs, but then Menzies found a level again, and that's something we don't see enough.

"What he should take away from tonight was the way he handled this situation. It was like he was there a million times before.

"He knows he can handle anything now."

Humphries vs Menzies: Tale of the Tape

Menzies to face 'Smudger' next

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player It was very nearly a debut to forget for Kevin Doets as he came close to taking a tumble on the stage

Ross Smith came through a fantastic encounter as he defied a 104.19 average from debutant Kevin Doets - taking out 160 and a match-winning 120 - to reach the second round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Doets hiit this 161 finish on the bullseye - just in time to save the match!

'Hawkeye' saved the match with a stunning 161 checkout but Smith held the Dutchman at arm's length.

After storming out of the gates to a 5-0 lead 'Smudger' kept his composure through a mid-session scrap before sealing victory - signing off with a spectacular 120 Shanghai finish.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Smith nailed this magnificent 160 checkout on his way to victory

Price wins in extra time to set up Cross showdown

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gerwyn Price nails the ton checkout to sink Martin Schindler

Former World Matchplay finalist Gerwyn Price survived a huge scare against German No 1 Martin Schindler to book his spot in the second round.

'The Iceman' trailed 4-0 and 6-2 before roaring back and punishing Schindler for errors on the outer ring to win 11-9.

"It doesn't usually happen. Without the crowd, I would have lost today," admitted Price. "That was the worst I've played all season.

"It goes to show, throwing sheep about instead of darts about, it doesn't help! It was a tough one for me. I've got no confidence at the minute because I haven't played a lot.

"To battle through it. Martin was just as rubbish as me, thankfully.

"That was one I should have lost, but I've won and I'm still in the tournament - I can't be any worse!"

Price will take on Rob Cross next after 'Voltage' kicked off his campaign with a convincing 10-3 win over Danny Noppert.

The 2019 champion led 5-0 at the break and never relented, averaging 97.41, pinning a 128 checkout, and ending with an impressive 52.6 per cent on the doubles.

What's happening at the World Matchplay on Tuesday?

Image: Luke Littler and Michael van Gerwen headline the World Matchplay action on Tuesday

The 2026 Betfred World Matchplay continues at the iconic Winter Gardens from July 18-26, as a 32-player field compete for the prestigious Phil Taylor Trophy.

Two-time world champion Luke Littler takes on Nathan Aspinall in a blockbuster clash after opening his defence of the Phil Taylor Trophy with a sensational 10-6 win over Niko Springer on Day One in Blackpool.

Betfred World Matchplay - Tuesday's fixtures [first to 11 legs]

Round Two - Evening 7pm

Jonny Clayton vs Gary Anderson Michael van Gerwen vs Dirk van Duijvenbode Luke Littler vs Nathan Aspinall Josh Rock vs Stephen Bunting

Stephen Bunting takes on Josh Rock after winning through a Winter Gardens classic against debutant Niels Zonneveld, surviving three match darts to edge past the Dutchman 13-12.

Three-time World Matchplay winner Michael van Gerwen faces fellow Dutchman Dirk van Duijvenbode, while Gary Anderson - the 2018 champion - goes up against 2023 runner-up Jonny Clayton having recorded the eighth-highest average in World Matchplay history, averaging 109.96 in his 10-2 demolition of Ryan Joyce.

Sports.title: Palace seek £55m-plus for Lacroix as talks with Chelsea begin
Sports.content:
Chelsea are in talks with Crystal Palace over the signing of defender Maxence Lacroix.

Sky Sports News understands Palace are seeking more than the £55m Tottenham paid for Jan Paul van Hecke from Brighton to sanction Lacroix's sale.

Palace and Chelsea enjoy good relations at the highest levels and they have done deals for players such as Trevoh Chalobah and Ben Chilwell.

Chelsea want to sign a centre-back and ideally any new arrival would be physically imposing and bring Premier League experience.

Chelsea have raised around £130m from sales in this window and more players are set to leave.

In defence, players who could move on include Chalobah, Benoit Badiashile, Malo Gusto and Axel Disasi.

Rogers arrives for medical ahead of record-breaking move

Morgan Rogers arrived for a medical with Chelsea on Monday morning, which you can exclusively watch below, ahead of completing a British-record £117m move from Aston Villa.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Rogers has been spotted arriving for his Chelsea medical after the Blues agreed a £117m deal with Aston Villa.

All being well, Rogers is then expected to sign a six-year contract at Chelsea with the option of another year until 2033.

Rogers returned from the USA on Sunday following England's third-place finish at the World Cup, via a bronze-final victory over France.

Chelsea moved quickly to secure the deal ahead of Arsenal, who were unwilling to match the asking price despite Rogers being their top forward target.

Image: Morgan Rogers will become Chelsea's most expensive player

Rogers will become the most expensive British player of all time when he completes his move from Aston Villa, with the fee eclipsing the £116m fee paid by Manchester City for his England team-mate Elliot Anderson.

Rogers is also set to become Chelsea's record signing, overtaking the £115m the Blues paid Brighton for Moises Caicedo in 2023.
