World.title: Volkswagen hires 100 sheep to cut grass at Polish solar farm as experiment in agrivoltaics
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Carmaker Volkswagen has deployed a herd of 100 sheep to keep grass under control at a solar farm that powers one of its factories in Poland, providing a greener alternative to mechanical mowing. The project, which is being run in partnership with a local university, will also contribute to research on agrivoltaics, the name given to the use of land for both solar generation and agriculture. Scientists will assess the impact of the practice on animal welfare and the wider ecosystem. In 2016, Volkswagen opened a major plant near Poznań, Poland’s fifth-largest city. The facility employs around 3,000 people and mainly produces VW’s Crafter van. In 2023, the company opened a solar farm next to the plant. On sunny days, its 31,000 photovoltaic panels can power the whole factory, though over the year as a whole it supplies around 25% of its electricity. Volkswagen has now announced that, earlier this year, it welcomed around 100 sheep to the solar farm. They are grazing on the 27 hectares of land around the panels as an alternative to mechanical mowing. “The animals adapted very well to the new conditions,” says Justyna Nowak-Gajek, the owner of the flock. She explains that the sheep are splitting into smaller groups and “grazing peacefully”, whereas herds that feel unsafe tend to stick closer together. Meanwhile, scientists from the Poznań University of Life Sciences (UPP) are studying the impact of the project on the animals’ welfare and behaviour, as well as the functioning of the entire ecosystem. “We are checking, among other things, whether shade created by the panels reduces heat stress in animals, improving their comfort and living conditions,” says Joanna Składanowska-Baryza from the university’s Faculty of Veterinary Medicine and Animal Sciences. “At the same time, we are analysing changes in the microclimate, vegetation and soil to identify solutions that facilitate the effective combination of energy production with agricultural activities.” Volkswagen has chosen Poland as the location for a new €1.7bn plant producing materials for electric vehicle batteries. The investment has been welcomed by the Polish government, which is providing €350 million in grants for the project https://t.co/xh0LuzHOyq — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 10, 2023 The study is expected to inform the wider practice of agrivoltaics, which aims to “create [solar] installations that coexist with their surroundings and bring additional benefits to the environment and local communities”, says Quanta Energy, the firm that constructed Volkswagen’s solar farm. “The photovoltaic farm now produces more than just green energy,” adds Marzena Pillich-Grońska, director of the Volkswagen plant. “It has also become a place where we support biodiversity, local agriculture, and the development of scientific knowledge.” In recent years, a number of Polish cities, including Kraków and Katowice, have also recruited sheep and goats as a greener alternative to mechanical cutting of grass on municipal land. Various firms operating in Poland have been investing in renewables to supply themselves with energy. In 2024, the largest chocolate maker in Poland, Mondelez Polska, said it would spend $1 million (3.8 million zloty) on solar installations at its production sites in the country. Successive Polish governments have also been seeking to bolster green energy. Last year, the country generated 29.4% of its electricity from renewables, up from 9.4% a decade earlier. Onshore wind led the way with 14.2%, followed by solar at 12.1% and biomass at 1.8%. However, in 2023, a group of business associations and international companies, including Google, Amazon, Mercedes and Ikea, warned the government that there must be more rapid development of green energy in order to attract continued investment in Poland. However, since then, figures show a period of stagnation, despite the current government pledging to accelerate Poland’s green transition after taking power from its conservative predecessor in 2023. World.title: Senior official under former Polish government detained over media campaign that attacked judges

A former senior official under the Law and Justice (PiS) government that ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023 has been detained and charged as part of a probe into the alleged misspending of funds. The case relates to the activities of the Polish National Foundation (PFN), a body created by PiS to promote Poland abroad. However, it spent 8.4 million zloty (€1.9 million) on an advertising campaign in Poland itself that promoted the PiS government’s controversial judicial reforms. 🛑 Dzisiaj rano na polecenie prokuratora Prokuratury Regionalnej w Rzeszowie agenci Centralnego Biura Antykorupcyjnego zatrzymali dwóch byłych członków Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej: 64-letniego Macieja Ś. i 63-letniego Cezarego J. 🛑 Śledztwo jest prowadzone w sprawie nadużycia… — Jacek Dobrzyński (@JacekDobrzynski) July 14, 2026 On Tuesday, the spokesman for Poland’s security services, Jacek Dobrzyński, announced that a 64-year-old, who can be named only as Maciej Ś. under Polish privacy law, had been detained. Maciej Ś. was a board member of the PFN at the time that the spending in question took place in 2017. Later, in 2022, he was appointed by PiS as the head of the National Broadcasting Council (KRRiT), a state media regulator, a position he held until 2025. Dobrzyński revealed that another former member of the PFN board, Cezary J., had also been detained as part of the same investigation into abuse of power and failure to fulfil duties. The spokesman noted that the allegations relate to the PFN’s so-called “Fair Courts” campaign, which he said “caused material damage to the foundation on a massive scale, in an amount of no less than 8.4 million zloty”. The PFN was established under the PiS government in 2016 by 17 state-owned companies, which provided funds for it to promote Poland abroad. However, the following year it launched the “Fair Courts” campaign, in which billboards and other forms of advertising in Poland were used to show the alleged failings of the justice system in Poland and therefore to justify why reforms being implemented by PiS were necessary. Echoing PiS rhetoric, the campaign suggested that judges saw themselves as a “special caste” and highlighted cases of alleged wrongdoing by individual judges, including one who had been caught stealing a sausage. (The judge in question had not ruled on a case since that incident in 2006 and had died in 2015.) In 2018, a Warsaw court ruled that the “Fair Courts” campaign was inconsistent with the PFN’s statutory goals, saying that not only did the adverts fail to enhance Poland’s image abroad, “on the contrary, they significantly weakened it, creating a negative image of the judiciary based on individual cases”. “The ‘Fair Courts’ campaign primarily involved attacking the judicial community,” said Tomasz Siemoniak, the minister in charge of the security services, commenting on Maciej Ś.’s arrest. “This campaign responded to a political order from the PiS government and discredited independent courts.” “The financial damage to the foundation amounted to at least 8.4 million zloty, while the moral damage is incalculable,” he added. “The use of the foundation’s funds for partisan purposes must be accounted for.” On Tuesday evening, prosecutors announced that they had charged Cezary J. That was followed on Wednesday morning by news that Maciej Ś. had likewise been charged and banned from leaving the country, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). CBA na polecenie prokuratury zatrzymało Macieja Ś. i Cezarego J., którzy jako członkowie zarządu Polskiej Fundacji Narodowej uruchomili w 2017 środki fundacji na kampanię "Sprawiedliwe Sądy", polegającą przede wszystkim na atakowaniu środowiska sędziowskiego. Ta kampania… — Tomasz Siemoniak (@TomaszSiemoniak) July 14, 2026 The “Fair Courts” campaign was just one of a number of controversial initiatives launched by the PFN under the PiS government. The foundation was regularly accused of spending money to support PiS’s political goals or on seemingly wasteful projects. One of its most famous initiatives involved the purchase of a yacht for almost €1 million, which was renamed “I Love Poland” and sent on an around-the-world cruise to mark the centenary of Poland’s independence in 2018 (though it suffered damage and spent weeks stuck in a port, accruing further costs). In 2021, the Supreme Audit Office (NIK) accused the PFN of violating the law by refusing to provide documents required for an audit. In February 2025, just over a year after PiS lost power, a newly appointed PFN board accused its predecessors of criminal negligence that caused damages of over 30 million zloty to the foundation’s finances. They notified prosecutors of potential crimes. Poland's state audit office has notified prosecutors of a potential crime by the PFN, a body promoting Poland abroad The PFN, which is financed by state-owned companies, failed to provide documents for an audit, but it argues it has no obligation to do so https://t.co/jEkjep9K9J — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 12, 2021 Maciej Ś. himself has also faced separate legal action from the new government, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, which took power from PiS in December 2023. The ruling majority in parliament last year voted to bring Maciej Ś. before the State Tribunal, a body responsible for trying state officials, over allegations that he abused his powers while leading the KRRiT. The motion against him included allegations that he unlawfully withheld funds owed to public media, targeted private broadcasters critical of PiS and failed to carry out duties required of the regulator. In response to this week’s charges against Maciej Ś., PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński called them “another act of vengeance by Donald Tusk’s apparatus of power”. Such actions “have nothing to do with the rule of law”, said Kaczyński. Their aim is “intimidation and defamation”. World.title: Five Legendary Ballets in One Night at Prague’s Hybernia Theatre
World.content:
Prague’s Hybernia Theatre is hosting a series of special evenings dedicated to classical ballet, bringing together some of the most celebrated scenes from the world’s best-known productions.

The upcoming Classic Ballet Gala will take place on July 22, 25 and 29.

More info about the program here.

The performance will feature students and graduates of the conservatory, presenting excerpts from legendary ballets including Don Quixote, Swan Lake, The Nutcracker, Sleeping Beauty and Le Corsaire.

Rather than focusing on a single full-length production, the gala will offer audiences the opportunity to experience highlights from several major works in one evening.

The young dancers will perform in specially prepared costumes and under the guidance of experienced teachers, including former soloists of the National Theatre Ballet. The artistic concept and dramaturgy of the evening are overseen by Pamela Morávková and Jiří Horák.

The programme will combine the dramatic energy of Don Quixote, the romantic atmosphere of Swan Lake, the fantasy world of The Nutcracker, the fairy-tale elegance of Sleeping Beauty, and the adventure of Le Corsaire.

Founded in 1945, the Prague Dance Conservatory is the oldest and largest institution of its kind in the Czech Republic. Over eight decades, the school has educated generations of dancers, choreographers, ballet masters and teachers who have performed on stages in the Czech Republic and abroad.

Its students regularly take part in international competitions and represent Czech dance at festivals and cultural events around the world.

World.title: Look Up! JAS 39 Gripen Jets to Fly Over Prague on Wednesday
World.content:
Prague residents will have the chance to see JAS 39 Gripen fighter jets flying above the city on Wednesday, July 22.

The aircraft will take part in a ceremonial event at the National Memorial on Vítkov.

The flyover is scheduled for 11:30 a.m. and will be carried out as a training flight connected with the ceremony.

According to information from Prague 4 City Hall, the jets will approach the capital from the east, flying over areas including Běchovice, Dolní Počernice and Žižkov.

The aircraft will then turn south over Prague Castle before continuing their return route through Podolí, Nusle and Hostivař. After completing the flight over the city, the jets will head back to their base in Pardubice.

The route means residents in several parts of Prague may be able to see the aircraft, depending on weather conditions and visibility.

Military aircraft flights over the capital are relatively rare but not unusual. In March 2024, crowds gathered in central Prague to watch a large military flyover marking the 25th anniversary of the Czech Republic joining NATO.

That event included five fighter jets and an Airbus aircraft, which flew over landmarks including Charles Bridge. The fighter jets later returned to their bases, while the Airbus landed at Prague’s Václav Havel Airport.

The Czech Air Force regularly uses ceremonial flights to mark important national events and military anniversaries, while also serving as training exercises for pilots.

World.title: Twelve Prague Tram Lines Changed Due to Repairs in City Center
World.content:
Tram services on Spálená Street and Národní třída in central Prague have been suspended due to track repairs.

The closure, which began on Saturday, will continue until August 10 and affects 12 tram lines operating through the city center.

The Prague Public Transit Company (DPP) has not introduced replacement bus services during the disruption. Passengers are advised to use the metro as an alternative, especially for journeys through the busiest parts of the city.

The affected section runs between the Újezd and Lazarská stops and impacts tram lines 2, 4, 5, 9, 18, 22, 23, 42, 93, 97, 98 and 99.

Several routes have been temporarily modified. Some trams are being redirected through the National Theatre stop on Masarykovo nábřeží, while others are operating via Myslíkova Street and Jiráskovo náměstí, or through Anděl and Švandovo divadlo. Some lines have received more significant route changes.

Two Temporary Tram Lines Added During Repairs

To help manage the disruption, DPP has introduced two temporary tram services.

Line 32 connects Vypich with Sídliště Řepy, while line 39 runs between Vozovna Žižkov and Náměstí Bratří Synků.

A new temporary stop has also been created at Malostranská. During daytime operations, trams will stop on the Edvarda Beneše embankment in the direction of Čechův most. During night service, the stop will operate on Letenská Street in both directions.

Track Repairs Include New Switches and Overhead Line Upgrades

The ongoing construction focuses on replacing worn sections of the tram infrastructure at the intersection of Spálená and Lazarská streets.

Workers will also repair track curves, install two new grease traps near the Máj department store, modernize two tram switches and replace aging overhead line poles near the National Theatre.

Additional local repairs to the tram network will also be carried out during the closure period.

World.title: Why Film Fans Traveled Hundreds of Kilometers to See “The Odyssey” in Prague
World.content:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey attracted film fans from across Europe to Prague, where Cinema City Flora hosted a sold-out 70mm IMAX premiere.

Tickets for the opening night sold out within hours of going on sale, with visitors traveling from several countries to experience the film as Nolan intended.

The adaptation of Homer’s ancient epic has been among the year’s most anticipated releases since its announcement. While its cast and source material generated significant attention, much of the excitement centered on its technical achievement.

The Odyssey is the first feature film shot entirely on 70mm IMAX film, making screenings in compatible theaters exceptionally rare.

Cinema City Flora is among roughly four dozen cinemas worldwide equipped to project 70mm IMAX film. Until earlier this month, it was the only venue in continental Europe with that capability.

Following the opening of new theaters in France and Belgium, it is now one of just three across mainland Europe still offering the format. It also remains the continent’s longest-operating 70mm IMAX venue.

Because 70mm IMAX projectors are no longer manufactured and require specialized maintenance, very few cinemas can continue operating the technology.

That scarcity has turned Prague into a destination for moviegoers willing to travel hundreds, and in some cases thousands, of kilometers to see major releases in their original presentation.

Set after the conclusion of the 10-year Trojan War, the story follows the hero Odysseus (Matt Damon) as he returns to Ithaca, a journey that takes nearly as much time as the war.

Borrowing from the Greek tradition of oral storytelling, Nolan’s nearly three-hour adaptation is told through the accounts of a bard (played by Travis Scott) who spins tales of the great warrior and Odysseus himself as he reflects on the events of his homecoming voyage.

World.title: Two Dead After Axe and Knife Attack at Prague Hostel
World.content:
Two people died and another person was seriously injured after a violent axe and knife attack at a hostel in Prague.

Police officers responding to the scene shot and killed the attacker, who had also threatened them.

The incident happened on Thursday evening at a hostel on Vídeňská Street in Prague 4, according to Czech news outlet Novinky.cz, which first reported on the case.

The hostel is located near the Institute of Clinical and Experimental Medicine (IKEM), and the attacker and victims were reportedly employees of the medical facility.

Police said the suspect attacked people inside the building before turning on responding officers. The officers used their weapons against him, and the attacker was killed at the scene. Authorities later confirmed that no further threat to the public remained.

Emergency crews treated four people following the incident. Two victims suffered cardiac arrest and rescuers immediately began resuscitation efforts. Despite their attempts, both patients died.

A third person suffered serious injuries caused by a sharp weapon. After receiving medical treatment, the injured person was transported to a trauma centre while conscious.

The fourth person involved in the incident was not physically injured but required medical attention due to psychological and internal complications, according to emergency responders.

Police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the attack, including the motive of the suspect.

World.title: A Night with Mozart: Candlelit Concert and Fine Dining in Historic Ballroom
World.content:
Few cities are as closely connected to Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart as Prague.

More than two centuries after Don Giovanni premiered here, visitors can still experience his music in a setting that captures the atmosphere of the era.

The Mozart Dinner at the Grand Hotel Bohemia combines a live opera performance with a three-course dinner in the hotel’s spectacular Boccaccio Hall, one of Prague’s finest historic ballrooms.

The concert features leading opera singers accompanied by a string quintet, performing some of Mozart’s best-known arias and duets from The Marriage of Figaro, The Magic Flute, and Don Giovanni.

The latter holds a special place in Prague’s history, having premiered at the city’s Estates Theatre in 1787.

The performance is designed to be more intimate than a traditional opera concert. Instead of remaining on stage throughout the evening, the singers move through the hall, performing among the audience and making guests feel part of the experience.

The evening is divided into three musical performances, with each followed by a course of dinner. Rather than separating the concert from the meal, the format allows the two to complement one another, creating a relaxed pace that encourages guests to enjoy both.

The menu draws on traditional Czech and Austrian cuisine, reflecting the region’s culinary heritage while matching the historic surroundings.

Each course has been carefully selected to accompany the evening without distracting from the music.

World.title: Prague 6 Wants to End Night Flights from Václav Havel Airport by 2032
World.content:
Prague 6 is calling for a complete ban on night flights at Václav Havel Airport, arguing that residents should have the right to uninterrupted sleep.

The district wants to gradually reduce air traffic during nighttime hours, with a full restriction planned no later than 2032.

The airport currently plans to limit night operations to 48 flights per night under its voluntary declaration. However, Prague 6 officials say the number is still too high and want stricter measures.

“Our goal is to ensure that residents of Prague 6 can enjoy peaceful and undisturbed sleep, which is a basic condition for a healthy and fulfilling life in our district,” said Prague 6 Mayor Jakub Stárek (ODS).

The district council is seeking a complete ban on flights between midnight and 5:30 a.m. by 2032. According to officials, the measure would significantly reduce noise exposure and improve the quality of life for people living near the airport.

The district plans to negotiate the proposal with Air Traffic Control, the national Slot Coordination Office, and the Ministries of Transport and Finance. A special working group is expected to be created to discuss possible solutions.

Prague 6 wants the number of night flights to decrease by at least 20 percent every year starting in 2027. Under this plan, nighttime operations would gradually disappear by 2032, except in emergency situations or other extraordinary cases.

However, Prague Airport has previously said that a complete shutdown of night operations is currently not possible due to capacity reasons. Similar restrictions are already in place at some European airports, including those in Frankfurt and Vienna.

Airport says it has already reduced noise impact

Prague Airport says it has already taken several steps to reduce the impact of aircraft noise on surrounding communities.

According to its environmental declaration, annual traffic has fallen from around 178,000 flights in 2008 to approximately 140,000 flights in 2025, mainly due to the increased use of larger aircraft. The airport has also restricted access for noisier aircraft categories during nighttime hours and currently coordinates only 48 flights between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m.

Runway closure has increased noise complaints

The debate over aircraft noise has intensified after the main runway at Václav Havel Airport was temporarily closed for construction and technical upgrades. The closure, scheduled until mid-August, has forced aircraft to use the secondary runway.

As a result, flight paths have shifted over different parts of Prague, including densely populated areas. Many residents have complained about increased aircraft noise.

World.title: Meet the Czech Superfan Who Dedicated His Home to Messi and Maradona
World.content:
In the quiet village of Bukovka, around 90 kilometres east of Prague, one house stands out from all the others.

Painted in Argentina’s iconic sky blue and white, complete with a giant Sun of May on its façade, it is impossible to miss. Outside, a life-sized statue of Diego Maradona greets visitors, while a massive mural of Lionel Messi and Argentina’s 2022 World Cup-winning squad covers the back of the building.

The extraordinary home belongs to Miloslav “Čurby” Urbanec, 51, arguably Czechia’s most devoted supporter of Argentine football.

Urbanec’s passion began almost five decades ago. As a four-year-old, he watched the 1978 FIFA World Cup with his father, who supported Brazil. But while his father admired Pelé and the Brazilian greats, Urbanec fell in love with Argentina.

The team’s long-haired stars reminded him of Winnetou, his childhood hero, and Argentina’s triumph that summer sealed a lifelong obsession.

His admiration has since grown far beyond simply watching matches. After returning from the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, he decided to transform his property into a tribute to Argentina’s football culture.

The mural features not only Lionel Messi but also head coach Lionel Scaloni, assistant coaches Pablo Aimar and Walter Samuel, and every member of the World Cup-winning squad.

Behind the house lies another remarkable feature: a private five-a-side football pitch inspired by Boca Juniors’ famous La Bombonera stadium. What was once an unused, swampy area has been converted into a miniature arena complete with terraces that can accommodate around 50 spectators.

The surrounding fences are decorated with images of Boca Juniors legends, reflecting Urbanec’s deep affection for Argentina’s most famous club.

The football theme extends to almost every corner of his life. His van is painted in Argentina’s colours and features images of Maradona lifting the World Cup alongside the slogan “In Messi We Trust.” One of his sons is named Lionel, while his attempt to name another child Diego Armando was politely vetoed by his wife.

Inside the house, Urbanec keeps an extensive collection of football memorabilia, including around 50 shirts from Argentine clubs, vintage editions of the legendary magazine El Gráfico, signed photographs and posters of both Maradona and Messi.

As Argentina prepare to face Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final, the blue-and-white house in Bukovka is once again ready to celebrate. For Urbanec, another World Cup dream is just one match away.

World.title: Trump warns Iran over US troop deaths
World.content:
US President Donald Trump said Monday that Iran will pay “many times over” for any American troops killed amid ongoing hostilities in the Middle East.

Pentagon: three US deaths over the weekend

“Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over,” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform.

This directive has been passed on to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman Daniel Caine, and “every Leader in the Military,” Trump added.

The statement came as the US continued to carry out airstrikes against Iran, with the attacks largely focused on southern Iran. Tehran retaliated with strikes targeting facilities and bases that it says are used by the US military in several regional countries, Anadolu said.

The Pentagon confirmed three US deaths over the weekend, including two at a military base in Jordan and one in northern Iraq.

The exchange of fire between the two countries comes despite a Pakistani-brokered memorandum of understanding signed in June to end the war and reach a lasting peace deal.​​​​​​​

According to a report by CNN, the US and Iran have considered a 10-day ceasefire to halt hostilities in an effort to prompt a return to negotiations, with the cessation in violence also including lifting restrictions on the Strait of Hormuz.

The White House said that diplomacy was proceeding along with efforts to make Iran “pay” for the recent deaths of US soldiers.

“Right now, President Trump is focused on making Iran pay for their violations of the MOU (memorandum of understanding) and their continued acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz,” a US official said.

“In addition, the president will make Iran pay for the recent deaths of U.S. soldiers,” the official said. “These devastating blows will continue until the president deems otherwise, but talks between our countries are continuing.”

If you missed it: Hungary lobbies Washington to avoid possible 100% US tariffs over Russian energy imports

Trump says Netanyahu ‘will not be arrested’ in US

In a separate post, Trump said that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu “will not be arrested, in any way, shape, or form, while in the United States of America.”

“He is fighting against the Islamic Republic of Iran, which recently killed 52,000 innocent protestors, and has spent the last 47 years killing American Soldiers, and others,” Trump added.

“The only ones that should be arrested are the people that led Iran into this unprecedented spiral of death and destruction, something that should have been dealt with years ago, by previous Presidents.”

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has told The New York Times that his administration’s legal department is actively discussing the potential arrest of Netanyahu.

“I believe that Prime Minister Netanyahu belongs in The Hague,” Mamdani said. “He’s a war criminal who has been charged by the International Criminal Court. And what you will find is that is an opinion that is held by many purely because of what his actions have wrought over these last many years.”

Netanyahu recently postponed a US visit originally set for this month to September.

World.title: PM Péter Magyar regrets Judit Polgár’s decision but accepts it ‘with respect’
World.content:
Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar said he regretted Judit Polgár’s decision not to accept a potential presidential nomination but would respectfully acknowledge it. He also took personal responsibility for communication mistakes surrounding the selection process.

Magyar published a video statement on Facebook on Monday evening after holding talks with Polgár, whom he described as “a living legend of Hungary”.

According to the prime minister, the chess grandmaster told him that, considering the circumstances surrounding the proposed nomination, she would not stand for the presidency.

“I am sorry, but I respectfully acknowledge her decision,” Magyar said.

He added that millions of Hungarians would probably agree that the country would have gained an exceptional opportunity had Judit Polgár agreed to serve as head of state.

Magyar praised her knowledge, international reputation, humanity and patriotism, arguing that these qualities could have made her an outstanding president.

Magyar says Judit Polgár acted responsibly

The prime minister said Polgár’s refusal itself demonstrated that she would have been suitable for the position.

In his assessment, she had carefully considered the weight of the office, including its personal and public consequences, before reaching a clear and honest decision.

Magyar thanked Polgár for taking the proposal seriously and praised the openness, directness and dignity with which she handled the situation.

Following their conversation, he said he respected her even more because she had shown responsibility, restraint, humanity and commitment to Hungary.

“Judit Polgár’s life, achievements and service to Hungary are an example to all of us,” the prime minister said.

Polgár, widely regarded as the strongest female chess player in history, announced earlier on Monday that she did not feel she had sufficient strength to assume the historic responsibility of uniting a divided nation. She nevertheless promised to support a future independent and respected president.

Prime minister accepts responsibility for communication mistakes

Magyar also addressed the criticism surrounding the speed and handling of the attempted nomination.

He apologised if communication errors caused by his enthusiasm and complete confidence in Polgár had contributed to the situation or influenced her decision.

“The responsibility lies solely with me,” he said.

The proposed nomination had prompted criticism from politicians, analysts and civil society organisations. Some argued that the process appeared rushed and did not provide enough time for meaningful public discussion.

Magyar acknowledged that events had not unfolded in a manner everyone would regard as correct or ideal. However, he argued that no selection process could gain the support of every citizen.

He said the government and the governing Tisza Party would learn from both their mistakes and the experience.

Read Hungary’s most important news in English every evening in one place: 

Tisza to continue searching for Hungary’s next president

Magyar insisted that the government had requested recommendations from political parties, public figures, civil organisations and private citizens from the beginning of the process.

He said Polgár had been proposed by respected representatives of Hungary’s cultural, scientific and sporting communities, while several other public and confidential recommendations had also been received.

The prime minister contrasted this process with previous presidential selections, which he claimed had been decided through agreements between political parties. This was Magyar’s political characterisation of the earlier procedure.

Under the current transitional rules, Hungary’s National Assembly will elect a president to serve until a new constitution is adopted. Magyar said the Tisza parliamentary group was expected to meet several times during the week to assess the proposed candidates before submitting its nomination to parliament.

According to the prime minister, Tisza will support a candidate who can represent the entire nation, possesses authority based on personal achievement and remains independent of party-political conflicts.

He said the party would not back anyone who had played a prominent role as an MP, minister or senior partisan figure during the divisive political decades preceding the 2026 change of government.

Magyar concluded that Hungary needed a president capable of bringing estranged social groups closer together after decades of political confrontation.

The search will therefore continue for a candidate whose integrity, judgement, patriotism and public service are recognised across political divisions.

World.title: Who is “Magyar”? The Ukrainian drone commander Russia has learned to fear
World.content:
Robert Brovdi, better known by his military call sign “Magyar”, has become one of the best-known commanders in Ukraine’s drone war against Russia. In recent weeks, his unit—known as Magyar’s Birds—has claimed a series of unprecedented strikes against Russia’s so-called shadow fleet in the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov, disrupting fuel deliveries to occupied Crimea and drawing growing international attention.

Why is he called “Magyar”?

Before becoming one of Ukraine’s most prominent military commanders, Robert Brovdi was a businessman. He was born in Ukraine into the country’s Hungarian minority in Transcarpathia (Zakarpattia), a region bordering Hungary that has long been home to a sizeable ethnic Hungarian community. His Hungarian heritage earned him the call sign “Magyar”—the Hungarian word for “Hungarian”—which he has carried throughout his military service, 24.hu said.

Following Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022, Brovdi volunteered for military service and quickly became one of the pioneers of Ukraine’s drone warfare. What started as a small volunteer drone team evolved into Magyar’s Birds, one of Ukraine’s most effective unmanned aerial units. He now commands Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces, overseeing increasingly sophisticated long-range drone operations.

How did Magyar’s Birds become famous?

Initially, the unit gained attention for using inexpensive commercial drones to destroy Russian tanks, artillery systems and troop positions with remarkable precision.

Over time, the force expanded into a highly specialised drone formation capable of coordinating large-scale operations involving reconnaissance drones, first-person-view (FPV) attack drones and long-range strike systems.

The unit regularly publishes combat footage that has attracted millions of views online and helped establish Magyar as one of the public faces of Ukraine’s rapidly evolving drone warfare.

The campaign against Russia’s shadow fleet

The latest operation has brought Brovdi’s unit into the international spotlight.

According to Ukrainian military statements, Magyar’s Birds have participated in coordinated attacks against Russia’s so-called shadow fleet—a network of ageing tankers and cargo vessels used to transport Russian oil despite Western sanctions.

💥 Seven Russian shadow fleet vessels hit overnight in the Black and Azov Seas According to Robert Brovdi ("Madyar"), commander of Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces, three oil tankers and four cargo ships were targeted overnight. In total, 183 vessels have been hit in July as… pic.twitter.com/xpHHvdSmdl — NEXTA (@nexta_tv) July 20, 2026

According to Reuters, between early and mid-July, Ukrainian officials said the operation disabled more than 150 vessels in the Sea of Azov and the Black Sea. Rather than sinking ships outright, the drones reportedly targeted propulsion and steering systems, leaving vessels unable to operate while avoiding major oil spills. Reuters reported that the objective was to paralyse maritime logistics supplying occupied Crimea rather than destroy ships outright.

If you missed it: Suspected Russian operatives held at Hungarian border ‘may have been plotting bombing in Germany’ — authorities tight-lipped

Why does the shadow fleet matter?

Russia’s shadow fleet has become a crucial tool for maintaining oil exports despite sanctions imposed after the invasion of Ukraine.

Many of the vessels operate under opaque ownership structures, frequently changing names, flags and insurers to evade restrictions. Disrupting these shipping routes can complicate fuel deliveries to Crimea and increase Russia’s dependence on road and rail logistics, which are themselves vulnerable to Ukrainian strikes, Reuters said.

A symbol of Ukraine’s drone warfare

Whether viewed as a military innovator or simply one of Ukraine’s most recognisable commanders, Robert “Magyar” Brovdi has become closely associated with the country’s transformation into a global leader in drone warfare.

His operations illustrate how relatively low-cost unmanned systems can threaten infrastructure and logistics once thought to be beyond the reach of conventional battlefield tactics, making “Magyar’s Birds” one of the most closely watched military units in the war today.

World.title: BREAKING! Judit Polgár rejects Péter Magyar’s offer to become Hungary’s president
World.content:
Hungarian chess legend Judit Polgár has declined Prime Minister Péter Magyar’s invitation to become the country’s next president, saying she did not feel strong enough to take responsibility for uniting a deeply divided nation.

Polgár announced her decision in a Facebook post on Monday evening, shortly after Magyar personally approached her about taking on the largely ceremonial but symbolically important position.

The grandmaster described the proposal as one of the greatest honours of her life and praised the prime minister for seeking an independent candidate despite the governing Tisza Party’s decisive parliamentary majority.

However, she ultimately concluded that she could not accept the position.

“I do not feel that I have enough strength to assume the historic responsibility of uniting a divided nation,” Polgár wrote, adding that she was therefore unable to accept the invitation.

Polgár promises to support an independent president

Although Polgár rejected the role, she said she remained committed to the goals associated with the nomination.

She pledged to support a new president who is independent, widely respected and capable of representing Hungarians across political divisions.

“I will do everything in my power to support a new, independent and recognised president in achieving these goals,” she wrote.

Magyar responded to the decision in a comment addressed directly to the chess champion.

The prime minister thanked Polgár for everything she had done for Hungary and said the country would continue to count on her contribution in other ways.

“Perhaps I can say on behalf of many millions of Hungarians that, even if in a different form, we will continue to count on you in the future,” Magyar wrote.

Reports of Polgár’s decision were published by several Hungarian news outlets on Monday evening.

Why Péter Magyar approached the chess grandmaster

The search for a new head of state began after President Tamás Sulyok signed Hungary’s 17th constitutional amendment on Saturday. The measure brought his presidential mandate to an early end on 20 July.

Sulyok had been elected by parliament in 2024, during the government of former prime minister Viktor Orbán. His removal formed part of a wider series of institutional changes introduced by Magyar’s Tisza government following its election victory in April 2026.

Parliamentary Speaker Ágnes Forsthoffer has taken over the presidential responsibilities on an interim basis while the government and parliament seek a permanent successor.

As we wrote today, two women temporarily take the country’s top constitutional posts

Magyar had promised broad public consultation on the identity of the next president. On Sunday, several well-known figures from Hungary’s cultural, scientific and sporting communities proposed Polgár as a candidate.

The prime minister subsequently announced that he would meet her and ask whether she was prepared to serve as president until the adoption of a new constitution. The parliamentary group of the governing Tisza Party also unanimously backed her potential nomination on Monday.

Read Hungary’s most important news in English every evening in one place: 

There was no public support behind it

The day after the heads of government made their announcement, Europion conducted a nationally representative survey involving 1,800 respondents regarding the nomination of Judit Polgár as head of state. The results are presented in the charts attached below; our main findings are as follows:

Among the population aged 16 and older, 35% oppose and 26% support Judit Polgár’s nomination for head of state. Opponents are primarily those over 60 (47%), those without a high school diploma (38%), and Fidesz voters (58%), while support significantly exceeds the national average among college graduates (33%) and Tisza voters (38%).

It is clear that the decision even divides Tisza Party voters: 38% support it, but 24% oppose it.

A significant portion of the public is taking a wait-and-see approach: 17% gave a neutral (3) rating, while an additional 23% were unable or unwilling to take a position on the issue, or are unfamiliar with Judit Polgár.

A relative majority of Hungarians (38%) tended to agree with the criticism that Judit Polgár “has no politically relevant knowledge or experience, and this is, after all, a political position,” while only 20% identified with the narrative that “Judit Polgár is a widely recognized, successful figure who stands apart from party politics, and therefore will be able to embody national unity.” Among Tisza voters, the situation is reversed: in this group, 30% tend to identify with the supportive narrative.

Nearly as many (27%) expect Judit Polgár to be “an independent head of state who does not shy away from conflict” as those (31%) who expect her to be “a more accommodating, conflict-avoiding head of state.”

Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced that he will ask Judit Polgár to serve as head of state until the new Constitution takes effect. Do you support this decision? (Population aged 16 and older, %):

A globally recognised Hungarian figure

Judit Polgár is widely regarded as the strongest female chess player in history. She became a grandmaster at the age of 15 and was the only woman to break into the top ten of the overall world rankings.

Unlike many leading female players, Polgár primarily competed in open tournaments rather than women-only competitions. During her career, she defeated several world champions and reached a peak world ranking of eighth.

Her international reputation, political independence and achievements outside party politics had made her an attractive potential candidate for a presidency expected to represent national unity.

Her refusal means the Hungarian government must now continue its search for a new head of state. The identity of the next candidate, as well as the timetable for the parliamentary election, has not yet been announced.

World.title: Fuel price in Hungary rises again: could a price cap return?
World.content:
The fuel price in Hungary is expected to increase again from Tuesday after another rise in wholesale fuel costs, adding fresh pressure on motorists already facing elevated prices at the pump. The latest increase comes as global oil prices continue to climb and only weeks after Hungary adopted new legislation allowing the government to reintroduce fuel price caps in extraordinary circumstances.

While no new intervention has been announced, the legal framework is now in place should market conditions deteriorate significantly.

Fuel prices in Hungary to rise again

According to Hungarian fuel price portal Holtankoljak.hu, the wholesale price of 95-octane petrol will increase by HUF 8 (EUR 0.02) per litre, while diesel will become HUF 9 (EUR 0.02) per litre more expensive from Tuesday.

The increase will not necessarily appear immediately at filling stations, as retailers determine their own prices. However, motorists can generally expect the higher wholesale costs to be reflected in pump prices over the coming days.

On Monday, the national average retail prices stood at:

95 petrol: HUF 595 (EUR 1.49) per litre

HUF 595 (EUR 1.49) per litre Diesel: HUF 615 (EUR 1.54) per litre

The latest increase follows another jump in international crude oil prices, which continue to influence fuel markets across Europe.

Could fuel price caps return?

The renewed rise in the fuel price in Hungary also raises the question of whether the government could once again intervene in the market.

In late June, the Hungarian Parliament approved a new law reforming the country’s fuel pricing rules. The legislation formally phases out the previous price-cap system introduced during the energy crisis, but it also allows the government to reintroduce temporary fuel price caps in extraordinary situations if market conditions or supply security require intervention.

At present, the government has not indicated that such measures are being considered.

Hungary previously capped fuel prices between November 2021 and December 2022, limiting the price of petrol and diesel to HUF 480 per litre. The measure was eventually abandoned after supply shortages emerged and several filling stations struggled to obtain enough fuel.

Read Hungary’s most important news in English every evening in one place: 

Hungary’s strategic oil reserves have expanded

Despite the higher fuel prices, Hungary’s energy security has strengthened in recent years.

According to István Akkapitány, chairman of the Hungarian Hydrocarbon Stockpiling Association, the country’s strategic crude oil reserves are now sufficient for 87 days, almost double the 44-day level recorded in previous years.

The expanded reserves are intended to protect Hungary against potential supply disruptions rather than shield consumers from higher market prices.

What motorists can expect

For now, Hungarian drivers should prepare for another gradual increase at filling stations as wholesale prices feed through to retail prices.

Whether the fuel price in Hungary continues to rise will largely depend on developments in global oil markets. If international prices remain elevated or geopolitical tensions intensify, pressure on domestic fuel prices could continue, while the government retains the legal option of intervening again if an extraordinary situation arises.

World.title: Hungary’s next president: two women temporarily take the country’s top constitutional posts – UPDATE
World.content:
Hungary has entered an unusual constitutional transition in which one woman is temporarily performing the duties of head of state, while another has taken over the leadership of parliament. The arrangement will remain in place until Hungary’s next president is elected and assumes office, with chess legend Judit Polgár now emerging as the governing Tisza Party’s preferred candidate.

Ágnes Forsthoffer, Speaker of Hungary’s National Assembly, began exercising presidential powers on 20 July after Tamás Sulyok’s mandate as president came to an end. Parliament has consequently appointed Deputy Speaker Anikó Hallerné Nagy to perform Forsthoffer’s parliamentary duties during the interim period.

Why does Hungary have an acting president?

Under Hungary’s constitutional system, the Speaker of the National Assembly temporarily exercises the powers of the head of state when the presidency becomes vacant and a successor has not yet taken office.

This does not mean that Forsthoffer has been elected president. She is temporarily carrying out the constitutional duties attached to the office until parliament elects Hungary’s next president.

Hungary is a parliamentary republic, meaning that executive power is primarily exercised by the government and the prime minister. The president is the country’s head of state and is expected to represent national unity and safeguard the democratic functioning of state institutions. Although the position is largely ceremonial, the president also signs legislation, may send laws back to parliament or refer them to the Constitutional Court, appoints certain senior officials and serves as commander-in-chief of the Hungarian Defence Forces.

Sulyok’s mandate ended after he signed Hungary’s 17th constitutional amendment. The amendment provided for the termination of his term after its promulgation, creating the current temporary vacancy.

Parliament appoints an acting speaker

As Forsthoffer is now performing presidential duties, she cannot simultaneously carry out the day-to-day responsibilities of parliamentary speaker.

The National Assembly therefore appointed Deputy Speaker Anikó Hallerné Nagy to perform the speaker’s duties. The decision was supported by 140 MPs, with no votes against and two abstentions.

Photo: MTI

Hallerné Nagy’s appointment is temporary. It will expire when the newly elected president assumes office and Forsthoffer returns to her position as Speaker of the National Assembly.

The arrangement means that, for the time being, Hungary’s two highest temporary constitutional positions are both occupied by women. However, neither appointment constitutes the election of a permanent president or a new permanent speaker.

Judit Polgár emerges as the leading candidate

Attention has now turned to the identity of Hungary’s next president.

Andrea Bujdosó, leader of the Tisza Party’s parliamentary group, told the National Assembly on Monday that the group unanimously considered Judit Polgár the most suitable candidate for the presidency, MTI said.

According to Bujdosó, a head of state should possess three essential qualities: dignity, integrity and empathy. She described Polgár as patriotic, honest, courageous and internationally distinguished, arguing that the former chess champion would be capable of expressing the unity of the Hungarian nation.

Polgár is widely regarded as the strongest female chess player in history and is one of Hungary’s best-known international public figures. Crucially for the Tisza Party, she has no conventional party-political background. Prime Minister Péter Magyar previously said his party wanted a president without previous party affiliation who could serve the country above political divisions. As we wrote yesterday, PM Magyar to ask chess legend Judit Polgár to become Hungary’s President

Nevertheless, Polgár has not yet been formally nominated. Bujdosó said the Tisza parliamentary group would make its final decision at its next meeting. Details: Tisza officially names presidential candidate as PM Magyar sets criteria

If you missed it: Judit Polgár nomination sparks political attacks

When will Hungary’s next president be elected?

The precise date of the presidential vote has not yet been announced. Under the amended constitutional framework, parliament is expected to elect a new head of state within 30 days of the vacancy arising.

Hungarian presidents are not elected directly by the public. Instead, the National Assembly chooses the head of state, making parliamentary support decisive.

Given Tisza’s dominant position in parliament, its eventual nominee is likely to enter the vote as the clear favourite. However, until the formal nomination and parliamentary ballot take place, Polgár remains a prospective candidate rather than Hungary’s president-elect.

Until the process is completed, Forsthoffer will continue to exercise presidential powers, while Hallerné Nagy will oversee the work of the National Assembly. Hungary therefore remains under a constitutionally regulated interim arrangement as parliament prepares to choose the country’s next permanent head of state.

World.title: 12 surprising American connections in Budapest worth discovering
World.content:
American connections in Budapest can be found in far more places than most visitors might expect. Statues of US presidents, museums dedicated to Hungarian-born Americans, pop-culture memorials and Cold War landmarks all reveal links between the Hungarian capital and the United States.

Some of these places commemorate major historical figures, while others celebrate entertainers who became American icons. Together, these 12 American connections in Budapest offer visitors an alternative route through the city – complete with precise locations to help them find each stop.

1. Columbo statue

Photo: Alpár Kató – Daily News Hungary

One of Budapest’s most popular modern statues depicts Lieutenant Columbo, the famously dishevelled Los Angeles homicide detective played by American actor Peter Falk. The life-sized bronze figure is accompanied by Columbo’s equally recognisable basset hound.

The statue stands on Falk Miksa Street, which led to speculation that Peter Falk might have been related to the Hungarian politician and journalist Miksa Falk. Although the actor had Hungarian ancestry, no family connection between the two men has been established.

Location: Corner of Falk Miksa utca and Szent István körút, District V

2. Ronald Reagan statue

Ronald Reagan appears to stride across Liberty Square in a larger-than-life bronze statue unveiled in 2011. Hungary honours the 40th president of the United States for his contribution to ending the Cold War and weakening communist rule in Central and Eastern Europe.

Visitors can photograph Reagan with the Hungarian Parliament visible behind him. The statue is also only a few minutes’ walk from several other American connections in Budapest.

Location: Szabadság tér, near the northern end of the square, District V

3. George H. W. Bush statue

Photo: FB/Zoltán Kovács

Another former US president commemorated on Liberty Square is George H. W. Bush. The statue recalls his support for Hungary’s democratic transition and his historic visit to Budapest in July 1989, shortly before the collapse of communist rule.

Bush famously addressed a crowd in rainy weather at Kossuth Square, where he reportedly abandoned his prepared speech after it became soaked.

Location: Szabadság tér, beside the US Embassy, District V

4. George Washington statue

Photo: Creative Commons

Budapest has honoured the first president of the United States for more than a century. George Washington’s statue was unveiled in City Park in 1906 following a fundraising campaign organised by members of the Hungarian-American community.

The monument symbolises both Washington’s legacy and the experiences of Hungarians who emigrated to the United States while retaining ties to their homeland. (Acton Institute)

Location: Városliget, near Vajdahunyad Castle, District XIV

5. House of Houdini

Harry Houdini was born Erik Weisz in Budapest in 1874 before emigrating to the United States with his family. He later became one of America’s most famous illusionists and escape artists.

Located in the Buda Castle District, the House of Houdini presents objects, documents and stories connected to his extraordinary career. The attraction also hosts live magic performances, making it more than a conventional biographical exhibition. (houseofhoudinibudapest.com)

Location: Dísz tér 11, District I

6. Robert Capa Contemporary Photography Center

Born in Budapest as Endre Friedmann in 1913, Robert Capa built his career abroad and became an American citizen. He went on to become one of the 20th century’s most influential war photographers and helped establish the Magnum Photos agency.

The Robert Capa Contemporary Photography Center explores both his life and the wider world of documentary photography. Its permanent exhibition presents approximately 138 photographs while tracing the defining stages of his career. (Capa Központ)

Location: Nagymező utca 8, District VI

7. Madame Tussauds Budapest

Madame Tussauds Budapest offers visitors the chance to pose beside wax figures representing celebrities, musicians, actors and other international icons, including numerous personalities associated with American popular culture.

Madame Tussauds Budapest, Hungary. Photo: Daily News Hungary

Unlike the city’s historical monuments, this attraction provides a playful and interactive American connection. Its central location also makes it easy to include during a walk between the Danube, Vörösmarty Square and the surrounding shopping streets.

Location: Palazzo Dorottya, Dorottya utca 6, District V

8. Michael Jackson memorial tree

An ordinary tree on Erzsébet Square became an unofficial memorial to Michael Jackson after the American singer’s death in 2009. Jackson stayed at the Kempinski Hotel Corvinus during his visits to Budapest, and crowds of fans would gather outside hoping to see him at a window.

Photo: lastnightoffreedom.co.uk

Photographs, messages, ribbons and other tributes are still placed around the tree by fans of the King of Pop

Location: Erzsébet tér, opposite the Kempinski Hotel Corvinus, District V

9. New York Café

Source: eventrend.hu

The New York Café has a more substantial American connection than its name alone suggests. The lavish building was originally commissioned by the New York Life Insurance Company and opened in 1894 as the company’s Budapest headquarters.

Its ground-floor café became a celebrated meeting place for Hungarian writers, journalists and artists. Today, its frescoes, chandeliers and gilded interiors make it one of Budapest’s most photographed hospitality venues. Read details: New York Café in Budapest, Hungary – The World’s most beautiful coffeehouse

Location: Erzsébet körút 9–11, District VII

10. Elvis Presley Square

Budapest named a public space after Elvis Presley in recognition of the American singer’s support for Hungary following the 1956 Revolution.

During an American television appearance in January 1957, Elvis drew attention to the suffering of Hungarians and supported fundraising efforts for refugees and those affected by the Soviet suppression of the uprising. Although Elvis never visited Budapest, the square provides an unusual link between the city and the King of Rock and Roll.

Location: Elvis Presley tér, at the Buda end of Margaret Bridge, District II

11. Tony Curtis and the Tree of Life Memorial

Hollywood actor Tony Curtis was born Bernard Schwartz in New York to Hungarian Jewish parents. He remained proud of his heritage and supported the restoration of Budapest’s Dohány Street Synagogue.

Curtis also helped fund the Emanuel Tree of Life Memorial in the synagogue’s memorial park. The metal weeping willow commemorates Hungarian Jewish victims of the Holocaust, with names engraved on its leaves.

Location: Raoul Wallenberg Memorial Park, Dohány utca 2, District VII

12. The US Embassy, Mindszenty and General Bandholtz

The US Embassy is at the heart of the most concentrated collection of American connections in Budapest. The United States has maintained its diplomatic mission in the imposing Liberty Square building since the 1930s.

After Soviet forces crushed the 1956 Revolution, Cardinal József Mindszenty sought refuge inside the American legation. He remained there for approximately 15 years, living inside the building until he was permitted to leave Hungary in 1971.

Facing the embassy is a statue of US Army General Harry Hill Bandholtz. He served in Budapest as a member of the Inter-Allied Military Mission after the First World War and is remembered in Hungary for confronting Romanian troops who intended to remove objects from the Hungarian National Museum. His statue was originally unveiled in 1936 and later returned to Liberty Square in 1989. Read details: The U.S. general who saved the Hungarian National Museum

Together with the nearby statues of Ronald Reagan and George H. W. Bush, the embassy and the Bandholtz monument make Liberty Square the most important stop for anyone exploring American connections in Budapest.

Location: US Embassy, Szabadság tér 12; Bandholtz statue opposite the embassy, District V

World.title: Tisza officially names presidential candidate as PM Magyar sets criteria – UPDATE
World.content:
On Monday, before the agenda was taken up, the prime minister identified unconditional love for the country as an essential requirement for the next presidential candidate in the National Assembly.

Regarding the presidential election, Péter Magyar said,

“We’re starting with a clean slate; we’re not bound by previous pacts or customs.”

He added that people should not expect them to choose a president from the old opposition or among Tisza voters. “They will make the right decision if they elect a president who will finally be the president of the entire country,” he pointed out, asking political parties and civil society organizations to explain who they consider worthy of representing the republic and on the basis of what values.

He noted that it is only natural that there will be no presidential candidate who satisfies everyone.

Péter Magyar stated that the new head of state does not need to be a politician in the conventional sense, nor does he or she need to be a lawyer.

For many years, Hungary was led by professional, highly experienced politicians and outstanding lawyers who knew the rules of power and the intricacies of the laws and the constitution inside and out, and yet they put the state and the law at the service of their own interests, he emphasized.

The President of the Republic must be someone who safeguards the unity of the nation and the rule of law; he or she may be a biologist, historian, doctor, artist, or lawyer, provided that his or her integrity and life’s journey lead us to believe that he or she can carry out this work with strength, integrity, perseverance, and love for the country—he stated, adding that the essential requirement is unconditional love for the homeland.

Regarding the presidential election, Péter Magyar said,

“We’re starting with a clean slate; we’re not bound by past pacts or customs.”

He added that people should not expect them to choose a president from the old opposition or from among Tisza’s voters. “They will make the right decision if they elect a president who will finally be the president of the entire country,” he pointed out, asking political parties and civil society organizations to explain who they consider worthy of representing the republic and on the basis of what values.

He noted that it is only natural that there will be no presidential candidate who satisfies everyone.

Péter Magyar stated that the new head of state does not need to be a politician in the conventional sense—in fact, he does not even need to be a lawyer. He cited Árpád Göncz as an example, noting that, in his view, it is not Göncz’s law degree, earned in 1944, but rather his genius as a literary translator and his humanity that have kept him in the hearts of many Hungarians to this day.

For many years, Hungary was led by professional, highly experienced politicians and outstanding lawyers who knew the rules of power and the intricacies of the laws and the constitution inside and out, and yet they put the state and the law at the service of their own interests, he emphasized.

The President of the Republic must be someone who safeguards national unity and constitutionality; he or she may be a biologist, historian, doctor, artist, or lawyer, provided that, based on his or her integrity and life’s journey, one can believe that he or she is capable of carrying out this work with strength, integrity, perseverance, and patriotism, he stated. He identified an additional requirement: the new head of state must be familiar with the country’s joys, wounds, and strengths; must view the country as a living community; must understand the weight of the spoken word; must be able to weigh matters calmly; must listen to differing opinions; and must recognize that every decision has consequences.

“It doesn’t matter whether they are a woman or a man, what their educational background is, what kind of family they come from, whether they are from the countryside or Budapest, or what profession they have pursued—the essential thing is that they love the country unconditionally,” he stated.

What we know so far:

Péter Magyar explained that they are asking the next President of the Republic to undertake “this difficult but noble task” during a transitional period, throughout the constitutional process, which will be nothing other than representing the entire nation.

In his assessment, Hungary has had seven presidents over the past 36 years, all of whom were elected as a result of political agreements, pacts, and party-political decisions. This had an impact on their acceptance, he noted.

“We have been given the opportunity, for the first time since 1990, to elect a candidate who stands above party lines,” he emphasized.

He asked both ruling-party and opposition representatives to regard the office of the President of the Republic, the independence of public institutions, the safety of children, the protection of public assets, the future of education, and Hungary’s international security as matters in which party-political interests must be subordinated to Hungarian interests.

Photo: MTI

In his pre-agenda speech titled “The True Hungarian Interest”, the Prime Minister outlined six conditions for the Hungarian interest: a functioning, independent, and just state; a strong and sustainable economy; knowledge; a safe and dignified life; national security; and national unity.

He recalled the Reform Era, 1956, and the period of the transition to democracy, noting that the greatest achievements in Hungarian history consistently emerged when Hungarians found common ground. He emphasized that the great figures of Hungarian history debated fiercely with one another, yet they always knew that the purpose of the debate was to move the country forward, and that there are boundaries that must not be crossed—not even for the sake of short-term political gain.

In his view, we are once again at such a historic moment today, because a long, inglorious era has come to an end, and the voters’ mandate was not simply for a change of government, but for a change of system.

The prime minister described the legacy left by the Orbán government to the new cabinet as grave, citing, among other things, the “historic” budget deficit, weakened public services, indebted institutions, and citizens who have lost trust in the government.

Péter Magyar identified a functioning, independent, and fair state as the first prerequisite for Hungarian interests, emphasizing the need for a public prosecutor’s office, courts, a constitutional court, a state audit office, regulatory agencies, and the office of the President of the Republic that protect the law, public assets, and citizens’ rights. He noted that this is precisely why they amended the Fundamental Law and are rebuilding the independence of public institutions. He accused the Orbán government of using the law to cement privileges, siphon off assets, and undermine its political opponents, while promising that: as long as Tisza leads the country, the role of the law will be to protect the community, limit the power of those in authority, guarantee fundamental rights, and ensure accountability.

He identified a strong, fair, and sustainable economy as the second condition for the Hungarian interest. He emphasized that Hungary welcomes any investor that creates jobs, brings knowledge, strengthens Hungarian suppliers, values workers, and respects our land, water, air, and the rights of local communities.

He stated that an investment serves Hungarian interests only if workers earn a fair wage, the community develops, Hungarian entrepreneurs secure contracts, and nature—Hungary’s water, air, and land—does not pay the price for profit.
